project.name: ev212 | EY Gov
project.descriptionHtml:
Welcome to GovTech radar!

In order to empower government resources to accelerate the adoption of new technologies and innovative solutions to shape the future of governance, the GovTech radar provides a glimpse into insights and research services that will be made available for government entities to help them conduct future scoping exercises and identify technologies for potential use cases and future solutions.

The present visualization tool contains 106 technologies assessed according to NASA’s Technology Readiness Level (TRL) as an effort to evaluate their level of technological development. From 1 (the lowest level of technology maturation) to 9 (technology is already being fixed and incorporated into new systems), all technologies included in this project intend to serve as a benchmark for future versions of digitized governance.

All technologies were analyzed according to the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) to strengthen the relationship between technological developments and sustainable practices. Each technology added to the radar was tagged according to its taxonomy, from software, hardware, systems, materials to business models and policies.

Ultimately, these technologies were clustered into seven affinity groups containing essays disclosing the most significant technological impacts produced in key public sectors, including Healthcare, Education & Training, Urban Mobility & Smart Cities, Travel, Tourism & Culture, Social Development & Justice, Energy & Natural Resources, and Trade, Finance & Economy.

You are now invited to navigate these technologies and explore the interactive visualization tool that helps trace a path towards a future government.
project.summary: Welcome to GovTech, an interactive visualization tool that allows navigation between emerging technologies expected to impact governments of tomorrow.

collections.name: Healthcare
collections.descriptionHTML:
Currently, when a patient gets a routine checkup, most medical systems focus only on treating diseases and combating the symptoms, normally discarding a deeper look into the complex causes of a specific condition. This is primarily due to the lack of resources or because patients cannot pay for the entire treatment. However, as people are starting to reap the benefits of data through online apps, access to healthcare information is changing, thus transforming how disease treatment and preventive care occur.

By combining comprehensive data with AI, an Automated Diagnosis System could allow medical staff and patients to deeply understand the development of chronic illnesses and find patterns that could potentially predict further diseases —and prevent them. However, even if promising, there are some challenges to overcome. First, the inability of the machine learning model to explain how it reached any given conclusion, and secondly, who will be responsible in the event of a misdiagnosis ending with fatal or near-fatal consequences. Society needs to determine who will be held accountable when something goes wrong. At the present moment, human doctors are responsible for each decision made by a machine, but with global data centers and potentially even global diagnosis and prediction systems, entire government systems could soon have to back artificial intelligence results.

Similarly, delegating therapy to an AI Therapist or being cared for by a Robot Caregiver demonstrates that artificial intelligence has conquered the last frontier of human trust, performing tasks that were once uniquely human, like caring for others or giving support. These technologies, which are genuinely non-judgmental, gather personal information and cross-data to deliver highly personalized care, meaning that machines could possibly understand the necessities of any given person better than another human.

Further in the future, someone could not only improve a physical impairment but augment the capabilities of an entire body with an Exoskeleton, thus becoming better than a regular human at desired tasks. Also, an Emotion Controlling Implant could analyze the chemical composition of the brain in real-time and act accordingly, releasing medication for mood balancing and eliminating emotions like fear or anxiety in specific situations. A person with perception impairments such as color blindness or deafness could choose to synesthetically perceive those traits through a Sensory Extension Device, crossing stimuli and likely developing new senses in the process.

Ultimately, with less dependence on healthcare centers, a Remote Hospital could become a popular alternative to a physical hospital, especially in pandemic scenarios. Also, a Healthcare Blockchain System could allow everyone to access the same standards of healthcare, irrespective of location or social standing. On the other hand, private companies are already seeing high value in data gathering; it is possible that only a small group of people would actually gain access to state-of-the-art diagnosis and treatment. In order to avoid this scenario, governments and decision-makers should pay particular attention to how they distribute technologies and the way they are later enrolled in healthcare systems.

collections.name: Education & Training
collections.descriptionHTML:
Since COVID-19, schools worldwide shut down, leaving around 1.6 billion students out of the classroom. So far, the education sector has changed considerably. However, despite the COVID-19 push to e-learning and distance learning, there is still insufficient investment and a lack of targeted training to educational actors regarding digital tools. According to experts, teachers’ skepticism about technological teaching and learning methodologies and lack of digital confidence are intrinsic obstacles to technology adoption in the classroom.

While the introduction of emerging technologies can bring a host of questions, the benefits behind its implementation are various. According to research, “[…] technology allows students to learn in a serene environment, it acknowledges the study of a ‘classroom experience’ without interrupting the established measure of communication, it facilitates students thought based on strengths and weaknesses, it aids the teacher to evaluate skills consistently and objectively,” and many other benefits. Also, from 2021 to 2028, the global technology market in education technologies is expected to "[…] witness a compound annual growth rate of 19.9%."

These recent events made some technological solutions race their development, such as Extended Reality (XR) Glasses. But this is nothing new. Before the pandemic, global EdTech solutions were already expected to reach investments of $350 billion by 2025.

In the case of professional workers, who are used to learning through hands-on experiences, XR technologies also hold immense opportunities. Expertise could be shared across any border, enhancing technical training. Also, Augmented Reality (AR) Workforce Assistance and Tactile Response Hologram could help compensate for cost-intensive purchases in machinery and consumables, preventing companies from buying expensive equipment before training their employees and from wasting processing materials during training. Beyond working environments, the same opportunities would greatly benefit exercises in the classroom, such as navigating through historical content in immersive ways in a Virtual Reality (VR) Classroom. This technology could also be helpful if, for example, social distancing is imposed. Both classroom and training experiences could take place even in remote areas or outside of schools, allowing learners to engage with digital content almost like in physical reality.

Additionally, according to Beatrys Rodrigues, there are even more inputs these technologies could offer. In her recent article, she discloses how XR representations could impact students' career choices by generating visual inputs that could be more inclusive and representative according to students’ personal realities. It could "[…] inspire the next generation of women, especially in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math (STEM) […] feel more represented through female characters. This could encourage and increase the likelihood of girls participating in both educational and professional environments." On the same note, technologies such as Artificial Empathy could significantly impact the relationship between teachers and learners.

Overall, technology can enable more efficiency in teaching and measuring the learning progress through the distribution of devices that could support and improve learning processes. From automatically identifying knowledge gaps and answering students' questions through prompt and pre-programmed answers, now teachers and education providers can reach their students more seamlessly, thus making classroom interactions more engaging and meaningful.

collections.name: Urban Mobility & Smart Cities
collections.descriptionHTML:
The complexity of urban development is deeply rooted in how the economy evolves. The configuration of cities often collides with strategic and physical planning, mainly because the approaches applied to solve problems vary from one urban setting to another. According to Jordi Borja (2001), a "metropolitan space is a perfect illustration of complexity," it is, "[…] a space of variable geometry; we do not know where it starts and where it ends, and even less, how it will be in 10 to 20 years. The territory is an outcome of an action, an outcome of a strategy." So, how can we design the best practices and strategies to deliver the soundest tools that respond to specific needs and demands?

To pursue better communication between cities and their surroundings, technological tools could help in this arduous task. Platforms such as an Integrated Operations Center, which reunites all data gathered by scattered sensors and cameras, can enable operators to follow changes in traffic, logistics, water and energy resources, food distribution, and many other variables. Through City Information Modeling, managers can assess a "digital version" of a city, such as in the case of Singapore. By combining big data, cloud computing, and Virtual Reality (VR), the city-state of Singapore can maintain a continuous laboratory for urban planning that enables agencies to act more thoughtfully when risks are flagged during a simulation.

By combining computer-generated visual models with AI, both Integrated Operations Center and City Information Modeling, geospatial data can be analyzed and thus predict the impact of climate changes (planned or not) in specific areas. Such visualizations could become assets for urban planners to deal with land use consequences in climate change, the flow of cold and hot air in urbanscapes, the detection of different atmospheric pollutants, and their dissemination in the air.

Technologies such as Automated Home Appliance could enable an improved infrastructure that makes day-to-day life more efficient and accurate at the household level. As appliances such as refrigerators, TV, etc., would be in constant communication and interconnection, household monitoring and controlling would be effortless. Also, a Household Robot Assistant would be able to identify trends and behavioral patterns from users by analyzing and cross-referencing new information with historical data and adapting in real-time, such as determining when to reduce home appliances' energy usage or doing groceries autonomously.

Regarding commodity, Local Delivery Robots may become popular in every city. Powered with machine vision, sensors, and GPS, these robots could carry heavy loads and deliver packages to remote or difficult-to-access locations, even in emergencies when the local infrastructure is compromised. These robots are autonomous and programmed to follow scheduled routes assigned by an operations center unit.

In terms of transportation options, current society has increased the need for more opportunities to move about. With motorized, carbon-emitting vehicles still the leading choice for transportation worldwide, it is high time to consider new possibilities for more sustainable mobility. Transportation solutions such as Hyperloop and Straddling Bus are expected to produce significant impacts on how people commute in the future. These technologies may decrease travel times and even reevaluate how cities spread. For instance, if it takes a half-hour to go from Riyadh to Jeddah, people may think differently about whether they need to live close to their work or daily commitments. However, the cost of travel through such modes of transportation is still unknown and needs to be explored further to understand if they will be sustainable.

Together with solutions that intend to change urban mobility and planning, further developments implemented by urban planners and governments must take greener technologies to the forefront of their strategies. Although the decarbonization of vehicles is on the agenda with the introduction of solutions such as Inductive Transport Charging, improving the energy efficiency of transport modes and vehicle technology alone will not have a transversal impact on citizens' quality of life. Technologies such as the Food Waste Monitoring Platform and Underground Waste Collection could help transform the citizens' mindset into a circular perspective and contribute to an increased sense of better living by removing waste containers from the street and avoiding food loss.

Smart cities of the future will perform massive infrastructure shifts that provide clean water, energy, and better transportation options to their citizens. Increasing the greenery inside cities would be a way of reducing waste while also purifying urban air, as plants naturally take in CO2 during photosynthesis. But besides plants and green areas, technological solutions such as Streetlight CO2 Absorbing, could not only help draw CO2 from the air but also illuminate dark locations and make them more accessible for people.

All in all, the technologies included in this cluster propose an urban concept that has the potential to contribute significantly to sustainability, as it integrates the goals of alternative travel with the protection of urban green spaces and the promotion of overall human health.

collections.name: Travel, Tourism & Culture
collections.descriptionHTML:
Nowadays, people can open a European banking account, have an accountant based in Asia, conduct meetings with Latin American entrepreneurs, and travel without leaving their homes. Half of the world is already connected to the internet and smartphone adoption rates are rising faster than any technology in human history.

Offline and online are becoming an arbitrary division in the 21st century, as the two concepts increasingly blend. Digital environments are helping the economy and citizens thrive and work together in ways previously deemed impossible. It even includes well-defined terms such as citizenship and residency, like the e-Residency, proposed by the Estonian government. Also, for individuals struggling to establish a fixed identity and access financial services, technologies such as Blockchain Digital Identification are helping people acquire digital citizenship in a blockchain-based system. Similar projects could offer full and equal societal membership by using new identification documents that would not be linked with a particular geographic region, such as the World Passport.

Projects like these show society that virtual worlds can be as important as geographic location. With the digital realm accessible by anyone with a device and a connection, digitized public services become available to a more significant number of people without worrying about the restraints of nationality or regionality. According to Kevin Kelly, this shift is "[…] the result of networks of communication expanding until they are global and ubiquitous, and as the networks deepen they gradually displace matter with intelligence".

The virtual and digital realms will become even more palpable as we use technologies such as Omnidirectional VR Base and Haptic Suit. Since they are precisely designed to help users feel and touch the virtual world, these technological solutions could integrate the layers of a city with digital data, combine information during daily activities, allow citizens to physically see future changes in their neighborhoods, and participate more actively in urban planning. By allowing the creation of virtual, three-dimensional models and immersive experiences to be accessed, XR technologies could create new opportunities for people to socialize, study, travel, work, trade and build the worlds of their fantasies without having to leave the comfort of their homes.

Also, Interactive Environments would allow any individual to live and experience different types of occurrences almost completely disassociated from the physical world. As this type of immersive environment combines physical and digital assets, it could be used to play games and interact with other people, both in the form of desired Avatar or with their “traditional” physical representation.

Also, with the rise of mobile communications adoption across all the different social classes in cities and the expansion of internet availability, future resources management may save a considerable part of the research budget by using data collected from citizens through Mobile Crowd-sensing Platforms. While the authoring front-end is used to specify one particular domain, the server-side of the platform collects information from users and derives behavior models with resourceful data. If appropriately used, city planners could take inspiration from citizens’ preferred choices based on the data collected from them.

However, physicality remains relevant. In fact, even traveling and border controls are expected to change. Automated self-service systems could be used to increase safety and efficiency at airport checkpoints, different from time-consuming current border procedures and controls. Automated Border Control systems would use biometrics tools such as face recognition and be deployed to help improve the flow of people. Through e-gates, passengers can cross through borders in a faster and less complicated way, simply by combining passport scanning and biometric identification, at departure and arrival times.

Ultimately, these solutions are promoting the composition of unexplored territories that exist as a digital layer over the physical world. People are increasingly interacting within these digital settings and devices, so we could expect that the concept of “reality” may even change in the years to come.

collections.name: Social Development & Justice
collections.descriptionHTML:
On the verge of a Fourth Industrial Revolution, governments are finding in crowdsourced digital platforms a means to make decision-making genuinely collaborative and inclusive. Online participatory channels, such as Emergency Citizen Responder, are increasing better engagement and more representative collaboration.

With more diverse inputs coming from civil society, governments and urban planners could become more conscious about people's issues. The construction of effective civic participation could help halt and predict disasters and deliver services to the most-needed places, such as the case of Predictive Welfare Analytics. Additionally, the development of the Real-Time Crime Mapping and Citizen Legal Support App offers more comprehensive means for law enforcement. Websites such as CrimeMapping make this kind of information publicly available so that people can be aware of criminal activity and the estimated risks for each mapped region.

Considering that trust is an essential element for the management of public integrity, the digitization of public administration could mean a new perception by citizens towards politics and the interactions between both parties. The technologies mentioned previously could make governments more proactive in the monitoring of crime rates as well as more supportive in the case of occurrences.

From a more preventive perspective, analytic and predictive tools such as Predictive Conflict Modeling and Programmable Law Enforcement, governments could take advantage of the data constantly gathered through these tools to offer more effective solutions for the welfare and daily needs of dwellers. In terms of transparency and the challenges of misinformation, public agencies can benefit from solutions such as an Algorithmic Bias Detection Tool to avoid programmed bias and a Deep Fake Detection Tool, designed to flag any occurrences of defamation or disruption attempts to the public welfare through the spread of fake content.

Finally, there are concerns about anonymity and data rights when governments use public and civic data. For example, GDPR’s Right to be Forgotten arguably clashes with the immutable and permanent nature of the Blockchain. Solutions for data redaction are being tested and could solve this specific hurdle. But a great alternative is to include civil society in decision-making processes, thus allowing people to feel empowered.

All in all, online forms of communication and engagement digital solutions could strengthen the relationship between administrators and civilians, thus helping create an ecosystem based on trust and interoperability.

collections.name: Energy & Natural Resources
collections.descriptionHTML:
The consequences of climate change have brought us to a threshold. Warmer oceans, expanding deserts, water scarcity, uncontrollable fires, floods, storms, etc.; all of these events have entered everyone's standard vocabulary. Ecosystems and biomes are crumbling, and some are threatened with total extinction. The leading climate indicators are aggravating, with figures escalating; in constant growth.

One solution to the general problems of air and water pollution, energy, and food insecurity requires a large-scale transformation into clean and reliable energy at a low cost, combined with an increase in energy efficiency. Currently, the cost of technologies such as CO2 Capture Power Plant and Atmospheric Water Harvesting is lowering—more than predicted by experts—thus increasing the competitiveness of clean and renewable energy. Additionally, materials used to remove carbon from the atmosphere, such as Biochar, are being developed and optimized, in some cases even being marketed already.

However, the conservation and restoration of natural spaces could be made more compelling through the identification of the protective functions provided by biological systems. It is not only through technologies that eliminate or transform contaminants present in soils, water, and air, that will solve all effects produced by industrialization. While trying to fix the human-nature ecosystem in the long term may pay back positive results, further patching of the symptoms of human-made problems may not be sufficient.

Technologies within the branches of Blockchain and Artificial Intelligence could facilitate collaboration between international organizations, allowing better monitoring of environmental variables, such as CO2 emissions and the tracking of industrial and agricultural practices. Autonomous Sustainability Monitoring, for example, could allow better auditing of countries concerning internationally agreed-upon regulations and increase pressure from below to fight climate change. All in all, the overall demand for transparency and traceability in terms of sustainable business practices appears to be the link towards a more transparent and trustworthy network for all parties.

There is no doubt that natural resource mismanagement contributes to the vulnerability of human systems and exacerbates the incidence and severity of climate-related disasters, thus highlighting the need for urgent and effective conservation or preservation measures. Current and future resource availability is a political, economic, social, and environmental issue that can impact all stakeholder groups and society.

collections.name: Trade, Finance & Economy
collections.descriptionHTML:
We are at the dawn of a remarkable economic changeover that promises better quality services and products, all due to the introduction of state-of-the-art technology within the branches of Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, Internet-of-Things, and many more. However, this transformation expected to deem positive results could also be problematic for those not well-positioned to reap the financial benefits of digital services. With the gap between the rich and poor at a historically high level, society needs to improve the methods of distributing the wealth created by technology. If not adequately assessed and distributed, it can lead to challenges of inclusion for our future generations.

Current differences in economic development, literacy, education levels, and lack of access to technologies are factors contributing to a widening divide. Consequently, the potential benefits of automation can be limited to those with better capacity to embrace technological advancements. Indeed, half of the world is still getting introduced to computers and smartphones, and education is slow to adapt to the rapid changes brought on by automation. Yet, while technology is making some jobs disappear, it is generating new ones.

The gig economy, for instance, is enabling more market opportunities for minorities, reducing the gender gap, as well as installing pro-worker laws. In fact, systems that take the lifestyle of a person as an economic asset, such as the Social Credit System, are allowing individuals to be more economically rewarded depending on their daily choices, such as if they take public transport or recycle properly. However, this model already showed to replicate existing biases— in new, technology-enabled ways.

On the other hand, as we mentioned already, technology is changing how individuals and entire communities exchange goods and relate to the products they buy. For instance, traditional supply-demand relationships and businesses are starting to offer products and services targeted to more specific personal needs. Driven mainly by direct and individualized interest, together with an increase in consumer demand for fair and sustainable products, companies and businesses are starting to adopt more sustainable practices instead of pursuing overproduction.

Furthermore, the mindset that there is a trade-off between environmentalism and economic development is also changing. Instead of hindering profitability, the pursuit of sustainability and innovation in business models and technologies could open up long-term opportunities for growth and reinvention of how to deal with available natural resources. Blockchain-based Carbon Credit and Waste as a Currency are great examples of how society is now taking carbon as a potential source of profit rather than a negative one, thus serving as a springboard to use waste as a resource.

Also, circularity is profitable. In Europe, it is estimated that the circular economy could save €600 billion annually and add €1.3 trillion in additional benefits. As for the regulatory aspect, China, for instance, once the largest plastic-waste importer in the world, changed its policy and is making the world rethink recycling. Additionally, governments in India and South Korea are even offering tax incentives for corporations to follow sustainable practices, with room to evolve into regenerative incentives as well.

However, business transformation is costly. Conservative industries are limiting, sometimes even hindering, the circular economy. Overall, there is little understanding of the circular benefits from a consumer’s perspective. However, the current economy, trade, and financial systems, accustomed to being oriented in a linear, consumption-based economic framework, are noticing that there is no other way besides transforming their businesses into a circular, self-sustainable economy. The technologies hereby included propose new ways of thinking, dealing, producing, and moving goods, always with an eye —and both eyes!— at the relationship of human activity with nature.

description.shortText: Autonomous electric robots equipped with a variety of sensors that navigate throughout urban areas or at indoor sites, monitored by humans who can take control at any moment, if necessary.
description.longText:
Equipped with GPS, an 'obstacle avoidance' software, cameras, and sensors to navigate their way along paved roads or indoor sites, these autonomous robots can safely and efficiently deliver items, equipment, and food. Monitored by humans who can take control at any moment, the robots feature a secure locking mechanism that would only open for the designated recipient.  

These autonomous robots range from suitcase-sized to medium-sized trolleys, and are able to carry up to 15kg of cargo. Deep-learning algorithms enable the robot to correctly interpret their surroundings, helping the device make intelligent decisions, and improving performance through experience. These robots can correctly interpret streetlights and signs, safely cross from one side of the road to the other, and identify obstacles or people to avoid collisions. At hospitals, for instance, it could deliver supplies, medication, meals, laboratory equipment, and other materials, allowing healthcare staff to focus on their value-added tasks. This solution also prevents employee injuries by eliminating heavy lifting and manual transport of hefty loads.

Delivery robots are electric, which minimizes the ecological footprint of local delivery, as well as freeing up valuable street space by traveling on sidewalks. In food delivery, these tools can get loaded at a restaurant with food orders and then drive itself off to customer’s locations. Alerted by a message, the client can then unlock the bot and retrieve the order. Large e-commerce companies can deploy these robots en-masse, as well as rent them on a subscription basis to both customers and local businesses. 

However, as the majority of cities are made for cars, this technology still requires human handlers. As the robot itself is only a component of an interconnected system, companies will also need a logistics system capable of holding a tremendous digital service.  


# Future Perspectives

Delivery robots can work in poor weather conditions, and they could become a popular and efficient answer to pandemic-proof delivery, protecting both delivery workers and clients from contamination. Besides that, as we move towards a more decentralized economy, companies of varying sizes are choosing to position several distributed storage facilities, instead of keeping one sole repository. This shift in logistics creates a suitable environment for delivery robots, which can only travel over short distances. 

Combining distributed storage with anticipatory shipping systems, it would enable a scenario in which local delivery robots could access a range of user-specific data to optimize the delivery of several products at once, saving both time and energy. It is also easy to imagine a scenario in which a person is woken up by a delivery robot ringing their doorbell. Without any advance notice, they receive an item that they did not choose. Users' consumption behavior would be tracked so tightly that the system would predict if they would be running out of toilet paper soon. The system sends out a delivery robot with the needed item in tow before the homeowner even realizes they needed it.

*Photo/Illustration: chesky / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Open flow hydro-turbines designed to harness marine current and tidal energy. By employing tidal current generators that harness marine current, kinetic energy can be effectively exploited and used as an efficient source of renewable energy.
description.longText:
Marine currents occur with greater frequency and consistency in specific geographical locations, making them more predictable than wind and solar sources of energy. In underwater topography (bathymetry), flow velocities in straits between islands and the mainland or shallows around headlands are considerably high, resulting in appreciable hydrokinetic energy. By employing tidal current generators that harness marine current, kinetic energy can be effectively exploited.

Many of the designs have taken a similar configuration to wind turbines, comprised of non-ducted, low-solidity, horizontal axis rotors. Such turbines are well suited to high sea-flow conditions, configured as ‘fences’ or arrays of turbines situated across channels at appropriate and energetic sites in the oceans. Open flow hydro-turbines with variable geometric blades are designed to harness marine current energy 20-40 meters below the surface in constant flow areas of the ocean. 

The most recent and advanced project in Scotland is predicted to generate tidal and wave energy for less than EUR 200 per MWh. However, devices that harness marine current energy face technical challenges such as material corrosion and high maintenance costs. In addition, these types of systems could potentially interfere with long-range power cables, the local marine environment and life, and the electromagnetic field.

# Future Perspectives
The total worldwide power in ocean currents has been estimated to be about 5,000 GW, with power densities of up to 15 kW/m2. As this technology demonstrates cost-efficiency, as well as high-performance and a smaller impact on the environment, more regions could harness marine current power as a more predictable and stable clean energy. 

Using a numerical ocean model, computer software could predict the movement of ocean currents. A recent study showed that the underwater turbines could slow down the ocean currents, leading to less vertical mixing of the ocean, reducing the exchange of water between the ocean bottom and the surface. Also, it is possible that these underwater turbines could also change the sea level, and, in some situations, this could help to protect the coast against future sea-level rise.

description.shortText: Software-based real-time information platform that cooperatively exchanges data between citizens, organizations, and governments to reduce reaction time and improve the effectiveness of emergency operations.
description.longText:
From minor criminal activity to natural disasters, emergencies take different forms. All these sorts of incidents put different levels of pressure on security services and emergency management. As current emergency response systems still rely on telephone hotlines — which can easily become overburdened in the case of an acute emergency —  emergency response units could help improve and solve technical problems of current methods. It involves the cooperation and exchange of data between multiple organizations, as well as, the affected individuals and potential volunteers in the area.

By using instantaneous mobile communications, including automated email notifications and instant messaging, reaction times can be reduced, and citizens can be empowered through improved access to information while also providing and updating real-time information to the emergency responders. The combination of the growth of the Internet-of-Things and the near-ubiquity of smartphones offers the opportunity to integrate these new data sources into an emergency response system based on crowdsensing; real-time data extracted from sensors and devices to inform strategic courses of action. Crowdsourced platforms might as well help to quickly locate volunteers near emergency scenes, reducing the occurrence risk of fatalities. 

Since decentralized systems are more resilient to single points of failure, blockchain technology offers a promising solution that would also provide interoperability and transparency. In terms of interoperability, blockchain can be adopted as a universal system across organizations similar to the internet. It would allow multiple parties across that system to coordinate resources in an emergency. Biases would be open for public audit as blockchain would provide a permanent record, which could be accessed by anyone, illustrating who designated which resources to a given area. 

# Future Perspectives	
The penetration of machine learning, crowdsensing, and IoT into emergency response infrastructures may lead to genuinely ubiquitous, connected, and automated delivery of public services, including health, security, transportation, and logistics. Machine learning could process and accelerate calls to dispatchers while filtering out redundant or less urgent requests. It could interact with callers naturally, instantly transcribe and translate languages and analyze the tone of voice for urgency. Furthermore, by examining changes in user sentiment on social channels, first responders could be given a head start, and computer vision could analyze unstructured data in photos and videos posted online to help find missing people.

The overall desire to deliver safer urban experiences to all citizens might finally solidify as soon as cities become able to address emergency actions with the help of real-time emergency management systems and citizen participation. These systems might be able to bring communities closer to the ultimate smart and safe urban experience.

description.longTextHtml:
From minor criminal activity to natural disasters, emergencies take different forms. All these sorts of incidents put different levels of pressure on security services and emergency management. As current emergency response systems still rely on telephone hotlines — which can easily become overburdened in the case of an acute emergency — emergency response units could help improve and solve technical problems of current methods. It involves the cooperation and exchange of data between multiple organizations, as well as, the affected individuals and potential volunteers in the area.

By using instantaneous mobile communications, including automated email notifications and instant messaging, reaction times can be reduced, and citizens can be empowered through improved access to information while also providing and updating real-time information to the emergency responders. The combination of the growth of the Internet-of-Things and the near-ubiquity of smartphones offers the opportunity to integrate these new data sources into an emergency response system based on crowdsensing; real-time data extracted from sensors and devices to inform strategic courses of action. Crowdsourced platforms might as well help to quickly locate volunteers near emergency scenes, reducing the occurrence risk of fatalities.

Since decentralized systems are more resilient to single points of failure, blockchain technology offers a promising solution that would also provide interoperability and transparency. In terms of interoperability, blockchain can be adopted as a universal system across organizations similar to the internet. description.shortText: A method that utilizes enzymes to break down sugar molecules and use them as a means to produce hydrogen fuel for vehicles. It is virtually as energy-efficient as traditional methods of extracting fuel from organic materials, and transforms vast amounts of agricultural waste products into energy.
description.longText:
A cost-effective method of producing hydrogen from biomass to generate fuel. The process utilizes enzymes to break down complex sugar molecules, primarily glucose and xylose, and turn them into hydrogen. It is virtually as energy-efficient as the traditional methods of extracting fuel from organic materials, and could transform vast amounts of agricultural waste products into fuel.

In order to safely and adequately store hydrogen fuel, the process could be carried out through electrolysis, where particles of oxygen and hydrogen are separated, and the latter can be blended with natural gas in an existing grid or stored separately in hydrogen fuel vessels. As wastewater treatment facilities look into generating energy as a value-added co-product, particularly where Microbial Electrolysis Cell technology is utilized, on-site hydrogen storage could become an essential and relevant consideration.

The defense and industrial sectors would benefit most from this application, as quick, low-noise vehicles that do not emit exhaust fumes offer a potential substitute for current operational vehicles. Urban mobility could also benefit from this technology. By only generating small amounts of heat and water, hydrogen fuel vehicles could cut down on pollution emissions, becoming an alternative to diesel-electric systems. Economically, this could end up being a more expensive option — especially for trains, which would require significant railway track modifications. However, with the falling costs of hydrogen fuel and batteries, the prices could potentially compete with diesel-electric vehicles.

# Future Perspectives

Hydrogen technologies still face significant uphill challenges in order to meet expectations regarding viability. Yet, current research suggests that these methods and techniques can provide answers to the decarbonization of global energy systems, thus incentivizing the proper deployment of this technology. Interest in this method is rising, following the conditional promise that hydrogen is well-established in particular niches, such as forklifts. This functionality provides a ray of hope that forthcoming solutions could replicate these systems, become mainstream, and also be applied to other industries.

*Photo/Illustration: By DedMityay / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A low-temperature brain or full-body preservation technique aiming to prevent molecular structures from degrading after clinical death of the patient by maintaining the stability of tissues.
description.longText:
A low-temperature brain or full-body preservation technique aiming at preventing molecular structures from degrading after clinical death of the patient by maintaining the stability of tissues. By replacing the majority of the blood with a mixture of antifreeze-like chemicals and an organ preservation solution, the patient could be cooled down to solidify and recover when external circumstances become more favorable.

The cryonics procedure takes place after a patient is declared clinically dead. First, 60% of the bodily fluids are replaced with a cryoprotectant solution that keeps the body from freezing. This step is needed due to the possibility of low reliability of survival during the conventional freezing process as tissue cells fill with ice crystals as frozen liquids crystallize, creating sharp molecular structures which break down cell walls as they expand, reducing the body to mush once it is warmed up again. Instead, the body is vitrified with the cryoprotectant, meaning that the molecules continue to have their intact structures but cease to move. At this point, the biological time is put on pause, and the body is stored in liquid nitrogen chambers at -196 degrees Celsius, waiting to restart its functions and bring the subject back to life again. 

# Future Perspectives

In the future, this human preservation technology could be potentially used, for instance, as a time travel capsule in space exploration missions. In addition, while being cryogenically frozen, people could wait in the hope of being reanimated by medical advances in the future when a cure for a specific condition is available with novel medical treatments. Similarly, people could have the option to potentially shift into a deep sleep option with cryogenics when they choose to receive highly invasive medical treatments such as whole-body resculpting and complete skin replacement, or even future holistic wellness treatments such as cellular rejuvenation, which might require specific metabolic processes to be completely shut down and restarted to take effect.

In a more distant future, to improve the safety of the process and avoid death, cryogenic preservation could be connected with mind digitization techniques to download the brain's contents onto a computer and secure the neural activities, memories, and feelings in case of an accidental malfunction.

*Photo / Illustration: © DM7 / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Through bright LEDs, machine vision monitoring, and cameras, this crosswalk disappears late at night and reappears as needed, allowing the street to adapt to the traffic flow and create safer areas for pedestrians while incentivizing fun and gamification of daily life.
description.longText:
Artificial intelligence can be deployed to make cities safer and more inclusive. A neural network combined with machine vision could gather data from several sensors spread throughout an urban area; this data could then be analyzed in real-time to classify and understand city dynamics. This system can recognize cyclists while detecting and responding to pedestrian movements and trajectories. The data is relayed to an interactive sidewalk that responds according to the individual's action. For instance, it perceives when a pedestrian wants to cross the street and creates in real-time, an LED crosswalk. Besides, this system would integrate cameras, sensors, LEDs, and other materials to interact with cars, pedestrians, and every other form of transportation to help make it easier and safer to cross the road.

The pavement would be comprised of a series of slip-resistant mat panels embedded with LEDs and held together by a metal framework to ensure that the panels hold up under the weight of vehicles and inclement weather. This design could help reduce the number of accidents at intersections and alert smartphone users about oncoming traffic. This system could also be especially useful in assisting people with disabilities and with reduced mobility to move about the city without feeling rushed by a predetermined allotment of time to cross the street.

# Future Perspectives

The gamification factor of this technology could potentially stimulate citizens to choose nonmotorized modes of transportation. It has the potential to make a simple commute to work, a fun experience. It would benefit both the environment as well as the physical fitness and well-being of would-be personal vehicle commuters, turned pedestrians.

Furthermore, as the ability to predict pedestrian and vehicle behaviors evolves, it could be implemented with Behavior Reward Systems to compensate cars and pedestrians for actions that benefit society as a whole.

*Photo/Illustration: Por Dinga / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A business model in which the excess power from renewable energy sources is available to trade between two or more parties across peer-to-peer platforms. Overall, it could improve social cohesion by allowing consumers to take control over their energy consumption and production.
description.longText:
A trading marketplace where the surplus of renewable energy sources is sold and bought by peers. In this business model, energy oversupply can be transferred and sold to other users via a secure platform, allowing users to manage their resources autonomously. In the case of energy deficiency, users can purchase the excess other users set available on the market. 

In order to take part in this business model, users need to produce their own energy, such as through domestic solar panels, or be signed up to cooperatives that enable users to trade the energy excess they generate. The physical structure can vary from traditional distributed-grid networks provided and maintained by an operator to local microgrids. 

This P2P network is divided into virtual and physical layers. In the virtual one, a secure connection is provided for participants to exchange all sorts of data based on pre-set trading parameters. The physical layer is a physical network that facilitates the transfer of electricity from sellers to buyers once completed the agreements of trading over the virtual platform. Currently, the large-scale deployment of peer-to-peer trading in electricity networks poses many challenges in modeling transactions in the network's layers.

In contrast to the current energy distribution model's top-down approach, a P2P design requires a market reformulation towards decentralized management, in which citizens actively participate in the energy market. This model's success relies on regulation and energy policy to design adequate market arrangements with appropriate taxes, fees, and supply systems to stimulate the utilization of renewable energy sources and mitigate environmental degeneration.

# Future Perspectives

Regarding the information system, it is crucial to ensure network security and accountability. Blockchain-based smart contracts and consortiums may offer advantages to amplify operations, as well as to secure them. When it comes to the grid connection, it is necessary to balance energy demand and generation. For that, smart meters need to be coupled to the primary grid to monitor the network performance. 

In the following years, energy security is expected to become one of the crucial issues to be tackled, not only in terms of sustainability but also of economic empowerment for small communities. Local P2P markets, in this sense, may hold the opportunity to improve social cohesion by allowing consumers to take control over their energy consumption and production while making better use of their distributed energy resources to contribute to the global energy decarbonization target.

*Photo/Illustration: Andrey Popov /  adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Three-dimensional objects, virtually projected in ways their design is shaped and felt by human touch. By creating an intuitive way of editing objects digitally, designers, architects, and engineers could use this technology for rapid prototyping and validation.
description.longText:
A tactile feedback system, powered by ultrasonic radiation pressure that enables humans to touch 3D digital images. Holograms release the visual inputs, and the physical experience is programmed through software using haptics. The user can sense the hologram because the air disturbances caused by ultrasound vibration provide sensory stimuli to human skin nerves.  

The visual projection occurs when a display produces 3D images by illuminating a tiny floating plastic bead, levitated by ultrasound in free space. The bead is moved at considerable speed, suspended in the air, creating 3D shapes that can be physically sensed. The disturbances caused by ultrasound waves are produced by an array of speakers positioned around the tiny bead, which allows tactile experiences.

# Future Perspectives 

Also known as acoustic trap displays, these holograms may play a critical role in all industries by creating malleable digital models' representations. Digital files could be sent online and then projected into holograms to be simulated and change shape by human touch. By creating an intuitive way of editing objects digitally, designers, architects, and engineers could use this technology for rapid prototyping and validation through a simulation model that could be tactile sensitive, working along with remote teams on product development.

By providing a shared experience of an object, this technology could avoid unnecessary travel and shipping. The user could download and experience the fabric's texture before buying a piece of clothing or trying an object in their home. 

Ultimately, instead of merely enhancing reality, this technology could enable the creation of entire virtual environments. Virtually created museums, classrooms, or bars could entertain and educate people, filled with distinct or even impossible inputs, such as extinct animals, foreign plants, or entire cities, enabling a more dynamic or alternative view of educational content. People could live inside their favorite shows or academic settings, and amusement parks with all inputs necessary to provide a fully immersive space.

description.shortText: A bus-sized ambulance designed to assist with accidents involving a high number of injuries, offering a wide spectrum of emergency surgical interventions. It is an optimal solution for cities with dense populations that require constant medical support and assistance.
description.longText:
A bus-sized ambulance designed to assist with accidents involving a high number of injuries, offering a wide spectrum of emergency surgical interventions. The oversized ambulance features a fully functional operating table, OR-light, surgical washbasin, and pre-packed and sanitized sets of disposable surgical equipment, ECG/defibrillators, CO2 monitoring, portable ventilation devices, infusion pumps, and suction units. 

These kinds of ambulances can provide total care and life support for the patient, especially for seriously ill or injured ones. Also, when hospitals face over-population, this mobility and medical model would supply additional assistance to medical staff, and subsequently attend a larger number of patients. 

# Future Perspectives

Although an interesting solution for cities with dense populations, this solution is not automated, which demands qualified personnel to operate them. Currently, governments and medical stakeholders will have to equally invest in human resources to make this solution relevant. However, if in the future large ICU ambulances are automated and self-driven, the amount of investment required in human resources may decrease substantially.

*Photo/illustration: ₢ Maxime Doré / unsplash.com*

description.shortText: Decentralized and encrypted protocols designed to improve the efficiency and security of digital health data, enabling data interoperability across different data points and enhancing the overall exchange of information and knowledge in a secure and tamper-proof manner.
description.longText:
A decentralized and encrypted method of distributing, sharing, and storing digital healthcare files. Cryptocurrencies and smart contracts, present in the blockchain, facilitate financial transactions and provide a solution to secure data in an encrypted ledger. 

Instead of a centrally located database to manage all medical information, in the healthcare blockchain system, medical records are shared among a decentralized network of verified nodes. Users, including doctors, nurses, and patients, can access files and add new data autonomously. 

Doctors and medical providers benefit from this technological solution by having more access to crucial medical data, besides sharing their findings across all users. By using industry standards related to APIs, this protocol improves data interoperability across different data points, such as continents and nations, thus enhancing the exchange of information and knowledge. 

# Future Perspectives

Medical datasets are a valuable asset, generally managed by private companies and institutions. By decentralizing and distributing knowledge across several nodes in the chain, healthcare data can become more accessible for all those implicated, such as patients and doctors located in areas that lack access to quality information. 

AI systems assisting the healthcare sector are gaining traction, meaning that the exchange of sensitive data increases exponentially. In order to preserve the integrity of the data exchanged, blockchain applications could ensure a reliable development of AI software, as well as improve the exchange of patient information more safely.

*Photo/Illustration: denisismagilov / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: XR technologies employed to expose patients to stimulating scenarios to treat phobias, traumas, and psychotic disorders.
description.longText:
Mental health treatments assisted by XR technologies. In this treatment, patients are exposed to virtual or augmented reality technologies to treat anxiety, phobias, post-traumatic stress events, and panic disorders. The XR therapeutic procedures can be done remotely or with the supervision of professionals, depending on the circumstances and needs of the patient.

Depending on the mental disorder, patients are exposed to therapy sessions through controlled virtual environments or augmented situations. In VR experiences, professionals conduct therapies in simulated environments that reconstruct past events for the patients to confront their trauma or phobia, or even recreate relaxation environments for group sessions. For AR treatments, with headsets or goggles, digital elements are added to the physical reality while the therapist provides constant interaction with the patient. 

Within psychotherapy, therapists commonly record their sessions through audio files, which provides no visualization of body expressions and emotions. As the data gathered from sessions is later stored in a dataset, therapists can visualize the undertaken sessions and access the visual inputs, providing better insights for doctors to understand mental disorder patterns. 

# Future Perspectives

Digital solutions benefiting the mental care sector are gaining popularity—therapeutic chats, automatic bots, and remote therapies through video calls. In this sense, XR technologies hold the potential to support the development of novel solutions that better engage patients and even promote mental care treatments, which for generations were considered taboo. Also, remote areas that lack access to mental health treatments could enjoy therapy sessions with stimulating environments tailored according to their needs.

description.shortText: An online platform where citizens can interact digitally with public services, making it possible to pay state fees such as licenses, permits, services, and other taxes on a unified system.
description.longText:
Digital and online platforms that enable citizens to perform state payments through a single website or mobile application. By allowing citizens to pay taxes, ranging from household bills to traffic fines, among others, it reduces operational costs, increases control and transparency, and lowers fraud risks.

This e-payment platform could also provide governments with simulations of the uptake of digital transactions. As a cloud stores all payments, analytics could predict whether an individual will be able to pay a particular tax based on the records of that person. While also delivering data management opportunities to help optimize both monitoring and prediction analytics, this platform could be used to allow citizens easier access to their expenses. 

Even if increasing overall accountability and accessibility between governments and citizens, this technological solution faces critical drawbacks regarding security. As it carries a considerable amount of sensitive data, it may be prone to cyberattacks and hijacking. As a solution, studies consider applying adversarial neural cryptography as a means to increase security and resilience.

# Future Perspectives

Many governments are currently working on programs to digitalize public services as digital adoption is expected to increase revenues and simplify public payments and services procedures. The collection and expenditure of public savings enabled by these repositories could help reduce corruption and irresponsible money spending by public administrators.

*Photo/Illustration: Teerasan / adobe.stock.com*

As a solution, studies consider applying adversarial neural cryptography as a means to increase security and resilience.

Future Perspectives

Many governments are currently working on programs to digitalize public services as digital adoption is expected to increase revenues and simplify public payments and services procedures. The collection and expenditure of public savings enabled by these repositories could help reduce corruption and irresponsible money spending by public administrators.

description.shortText: An electrical brain implant capable of controlling psychiatric conditions, including addiction, depression, and borderline personality disorder.
description.longText:
Current methods to alter or even enhance the human condition and mood involving recreational drugs and pharmaceuticals are already available. However, they also have several collateral side effects due to their chemical compounds and their vague target approach. It means that when a person ingests a drug, it has to travel through the blood system and be sprayed onto the entire brain, not only the neurons that are targeted. 

A new solution could be found in the creation of brain implants that can change the actual brain chemistry via wireless remote control. This technique is known as deep-brain stimulation and consists of sending short electrical pulses that could alter neural activity. This technology would be able to target specific cells and switch them on and off, enabling the control of psychiatric conditions, including addiction, depression, and borderline personality disorder. It has been proven to treat Parkinson’s disease successfully, and brain cancer patients could also take advantage of an implant, as it would likely have very few side effects.

On the other hand, the US military has begun testing AI mood-altering brain implants to promote deep brain stimulation among soldiers. Mental illness among veterans is a widespread issue in the army, and suicide rates are three times higher compared to the general public. Accordingly, helping these soldiers develop a more controlled, steady method to combat might help them mitigate the side effects of experiencing such hostile environments.

# Future Perspectives

Besides the challenge of needing to fully understand how the human brain works, another concern that arises with the possibility of developing this kind of technology is regarding the ethical impact it carries. Neurodivergent individuals could be encouraged to use these implants to fit inside social constructs and brain function norms. The use of pharmaceuticals (mostly anti-depressives) is already questioned along these same lines. 

Having emotions remotely controlled could bring up additional concerns about the construction of human personality, as the issue could be interpreted as something abnormal in human beings. The desire to control human emotions might lead to a dystopian scenario of crowd control enforced by technological means. No diversity would be tolerated, and any simple mistake could have severe consequences when individuals step out the prescribed behaviors.

description.shortText: Solar-powered streetlights equipped with CO2 scrubbers that help absorb pollutants present in the atmosphere. While generating light, this solution can mitigate fossil fuel contamination effortlessly.
description.longText:
Directional LED streetlights, combined with an Air Purification System (APS), designed to remove CO2 from the surrounding environment. While generating light, this solution can mitigate fossil fuel contamination effortlessly. 

Intakes positioned in the center of the lamp structure suck in polluted air through a purification system. Air pollutants are transported down along a small duct, while gravity draws the contaminants to the bottom. After purification, the air is released through the ducts and sent back into circulation. 

The mechanism comes integrated with solar panels that are responsible for powering lights and recharging batteries during the daytime for the night operation. Integrated with monitoring systems, these lamps are capable of communicating to a central station reporting operation performance, as well as notifying when repairs are needed.

# Future Perspectives 

This technology holds great potential for scalability and applicability. As streetlights can be replicated at scale and scattered throughout the city, this solution can both light up cities sustainably and contain CO2 emissions in urban areas simultaneously. Also, local governments could reduce urban CO2 emissions by creating taxes addressed to fossil fuel vehicles by asking car owners to commission a number of purifying streetlamps equivalently to the pollution their automobiles produce.

description.shortText: Software powered by machine learning that combines technical knowledge with judiciary systems to detect, identify, and predict illicit activities and audit public accounts and assets, including cryptocurrencies.
description.longText:
Automated compliance software combines technical knowledge with judiciary systems to detect and prevent criminal activity through the social management of public administration. Embedded with machine learning, it would help identify illicit activity and audit public accounts and assets, including cryptocurrencies.

By combing through millions of transactions within public and private data, algorithms could identify expenditures or illegal operations, bringing sweeping changes to the financial and regulatory landscapes. The immense amount of data processing and pattern recognition achievable through machine learning has the potential to red flag corruption schemes and hold governments accountable like never before. Besides, this automated panorama could mean the improvement of many aspects of government-related functions such as legal research, outcome prediction, contract review, and fraud detection. 

Government agencies, institutions, and companies could make these audits public, aiding anyone who may want to investigate or help create more regulatory processes. In this sense, social media plays a key role in keeping citizens abreast of posts that expose dishonesty. Therefore, the population would be able to mobilize and lodge complaints en masse, and maybe even put pressure on public agencies to obligate the use of automated compliance methods across all systems.

# Future Perspectives

Although the topic of sustainability is gaining increasing political, social, and economic significance, current business practices are adapting slowly, partly due to the ever-growing number of regulations, norms, and certifications. Automated solutions could help with enforcement but also allow organizations to self-monitor more effectively. The limited spread of software and standardized exchange formats for environmental data constitute a significant obstacle to this process. Determining how best to codify environmental regulations is an area of active research that could be expanded upon using blockchain technology with the help of smart contracts.

The automation of compliance could change the whole regulatory landscape, making it almost impossible to fake expenditures. As audits become public, compliance also transforms into a social phenomenon and ceases to be an "agency-exclusive" issue. Anyone would be able to create a bot to audit the government or companies; the source code would be open for public use and more accessible to the general population, which in turn could endanger privacy and the right to secrecy of citizens. At the same time, transparency and data sharing would serve society as a whole. Also, the pressure could force public services to go digital, making the government rush to turn all their information into a machine-readable format. In a smart future, with the appliance of deep-learning techniques, such as artificial neural networks, systems might be able to predict intention and read politicians' behavior, thus avoiding political crimes committed against the population.

description.shortText: A robotic powered with machine vision that recognizes, sorts, picks, and processes debris for recycling. It helps in handling sudden shifts in waste volumes, but also makes the reuse of domestic and industrial waste more efficient by inserting leftover materials back into the supply chain.
description.longText:
Robotic machines powered by machine vision and equipped with sensors designed to visually identify different types of materials present in the waste, making recycling more manageable and efficient. These automatic machines sort, pick and place items at a speed of over 100 pieces per minute. The platform can distinguish materials by color, clarity, and opacity, along with other factors, as they pass through a conveyor belt.

These robots are employed at any part of the waste collection chain, such as wastewater pipelines, waste treatment plants, or industrial facilities that process considerable amounts of debris. Because it is powered by machine vision, the robots can target and process a vast range of metals, components, plastics, and more. Searching for a better solution to maximize the recovery of materials present in streams, these systems could be used for recovering electronic waste due to their ability to detect even the smallest components. 

# Future Perspectives

The demand for recycling increases as the global population grows, as well as in specific situations, such as during pandemic crises or after large-scale catastrophes. This smart robot could play a pivotal role in handling sudden shifts in waste volumes while avoiding human contact with waste. Also, it could make the reuse of domestic and industrial waste more efficient by reinserting the leftover materials back into the supply chain, mitigating the shortage of necessary products.

description.shortText: An elevated mass transit system designed for dense urban corridors in which a vehicle straddles the width of two road lanes, bypassing traffic congestion. The electric-powered vehicle has the capacity to replace up to 40 conventional buses and overall has improved energy efficiency.
description.longText:
An elevated mass transit vehicle that runs along fixed routes in dense urban corridors. It is designed to cost a fraction of subway construction prices while being able to replace up to 40 conventional buses. The bus straddles the width of two road lanes and uses the airspace above highways to bypass traffic congestion. 

The vehicle runs on rails, and it is powered by electric engines using the power lines overhead and supplemented by onboard batteries and supercapacitors. It is equipped with warning lights to prevent tall vehicles from attempting to pass underneath and causing an accident. It also has sensors to keep it from colliding with an object on the way. Larger versions are articulated to facilitate curves over existing road infrastructure. In cases of emergency, it has inflatable evacuation slides similar to aircraft.

# Future Perspectives

Even if promising, this solution is costly and will face implementation hurdles considering current urban plans. In European cities, for instance, urban infrastructure is not as ample for the implementation of a straddling bus, and the only viable option would be roads or larger routes with considerable more space. In big cities lacking access to public transport, such as in the Americas, this technological solution would deem very positive results, such as providing to citizens with additional transport options.

description.shortText: A vertical Skyport used by electric aircraft for recharging and delivering passengers or goods for further on-land delivery. This technology is expected to decrease traffic congestions and improve overall urban mobility densities.
description.longText:
A vertical port destined for landing and takeoff of electric aircraft. By retrofitting its design, existing buildings, rooftops, railway stations, parking lots, or other city locations could accommodate this platform. The skyport would be coupled with recharging pads powered both by wind and solar energy, thus offering a sustainable alternative to fossil fuel vehicles.

The skyport would be connected with an operations control center, ensuring the aircraft's landing and takeoff are synced with overall air traffic. In wide-ranging infrastructures, they could house an extensive range of electric aircraft, such as electric helicopters, airborne taxis, uncrewed aircraft, and drones. Besides, through partnerships with landlords, local governments, and large property owners, this model could be located on different sites around the city. 

# Future Perspectives

Cities worldwide are already equipped with several helipads using skyscrapers as the foundation for their structure. By utilizing already existing structures in urban settings, the costs of electric aircraft skyports implementation could be kept low, thus improving these projects' chances of scalability citywide.

*Photo/Illustration: chesky / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A decentralized model of care that combines real-time data analytics and remote diagnosis as an alternative to current hospitalization systems.
description.longText:
Technologies such as real-time video communication can help remove the barriers of space and time between patients, including the time spent traveling to and from a healthcare provider. A remote hospital, which is based on a decentralized model of care, is intended to diagnose conditions and treat patients in their own homes. It could become a substitute for face-to-face consultations and help make collaboration between health care professionals more accessible. 

Although technology has been improving and gaining visibility throughout the globe, doctors are still predominantly treating patients during in-person clinical encounters. Currently, socio-economic and medical factors are causing a growing divide in mortality, and the best doctors and providers are drawn to top hospitals in the most desirable places instead of existing in areas of most need. 

With advancements in biosensing technology continuously tracking data such as heart rate, skin temperature, body posture, and many other statistics, even complex conditions could be diagnosed remotely. Apart from reducing hospitalization costs, improving convenience, and comfort for the patient, it could serve as an alternative method in countries where access to hospital services in rural or remote areas is difficult or nearly unavailable. In pandemic crises, this technology would be especially useful to preserve the medical system and to attend and supply the needs of a whole community. 

Through decentralization of hospital services, access to medical experts could be democratized, but decentralization requires cross-organizational protocols for data sharing that improves communication and more actively engages patients (and their families) in their care. Besides, widespread adoption requires new payment models and involves creating a market in which patients consume healthcare services more similarly to traditional goods and services. 

# Future Perspectives

As with other industries, the availability of online information and resources has enabled patients to take a more pro-active role in managing their health and make decisions that previously required visits to highly trained professionals. Person-centered healthcare, and available remotely irrespective of location, would not only require functional changes in the way hospitalization and treatment are handled but also requires improved health-related education to allow the patient to take a more proactive role in their treatment.

The decentralization of healthcare and the increasing prevalence of personal biosensors are creating the need for decentralized databases to store immense amounts of data while guaranteeing patient privacy. More machine-readable data would allow remote human experts to be replaced or augmented with expert systems involving machine learning. Machine learning models could incorporate the knowledge of a multitude of experts, potentially amplifying collective crowd wisdom. In the future, our own bathroom could become the doctor’s office, likely counting on the collective expertise of the world’s leading doctors.

description.shortText: Labels added to the packaging of products, indicating the sustainability level concerning the human, social, economic, and environmental impacts behind manufacturing practices.
description.longText:
Quality control labels that issue the sustainability level behind the manufacturing practices of products. This labeling model accounts for companies and institutions that comply with basic requirements following ethical practices concerning their human, non-human, social, economic, and environmental impact. 

When labeled, a product complies with several criteria, verified by trained professionals who pay periodic visits to industrial or supply chain facilities to validate their processes according to a standard methodology. For instance, a farmer who complies with regenerative practices, such as not applying toxic fertilizers and not using child labor, could access a specific certification. In turn, he could sell his produce for a fairer price to companies who want to comply with these criteria. 

Current regulatory efforts are working on expanding the limits of ethical product labeling. This system is commonly found and mostly limited to alimentary products, such as coffee and chocolate or personal care products, with non-toxic ingredients, cruelty-free or vegan certifications. Proposals range from certifying quality control tags to each part of the supply chain of multinational companies, as well as governments and institutions regarding their social accountability. 

# Future Perspectives

With blockchain, certification processes could be easily automated, better synchronized, more transparent, and harder to tamper with. Each step in the supply chain would be monitored and registered in the blockchain, thus adding value to certified products.

description.shortText: Robots powered by machine learning and machine vision, designed to monitor and assist the elderly and people with disabilities in performing daily tasks.
description.longText:
Robots, powered by machine learning and machine vision, designed to monitor and assist the elderly and people with disabilities while undertaking daily tasks. The robots are pre-programmed with a set of algorithms that learn and adapt their actions according to the specific needs of each patient, providing tailored services that are developed by understanding gestures, verbal, and non-verbal cues.

The deployment of machine learning technology enables the robot to estimate human poses and expressions. By learning behavior patterns, robots improve activity suggestions based on each individual. Services include providing all-inclusive care from bed to wheelchair by doing the heavy lifting, assisting with bathroom needs, preparing and serving meals, and dispensing medication. Apart from these applications, these robots can help suppress emotional needs by providing companionship, assisting therapists in further treatments such as depression, phobia, and post-traumatic disorders. 

# Future Perspectives

The deployment of automated robots in the healthcare sector is increasing exponentially. Currently, robots still perform limited tasks and are not able to conduct high demanding activities that require more attention and meticulous care. 

Yet, as AI-based systems are gaining traction and evolving at unprecedented speeds, the likelihood of substituting medical staff with robot caregivers raises proportionally. By automating the healthcare sector, it can either allocate the current personnel to more specialized tasks, such as research and monitoring, but also provoke massive lay-offs and employment crises. To avoid such a scenario, governments and institutions should create policies and training practices in advance. 

*Photo/Illustration: M.Dörr & M.Frommherz / adobe.stock.com*
