description.shortText: An injectable material that promotes the regeneration of skin and tissue to heal wounds by favoring the growth of new cells. It has a wide range of applications, from acute damage, like lacerations and surgical wound closures, to more chronic wounds, like diabetic ulcers.
description.longText:
An injectable material promoting the regeneration of skin and tissue to heal wounds by favoring the growth of new cells. Combining chemicals and adapted spherical microfluidics, the gel creates a scaffolding-type structure that allows rapid new tissue growth in the voids between the microspheres until the wound is completely healed. The material can be useful for a wide range of wound applications, from acute damage, like lacerations and surgical wound closures, to more chronic applications, like diabetic ulcers and large surface area burns.

Among the applications of regenerative aesthetic dermatology, which focuses on innovative treatments to support the skin in restoring and regenerating old and/or damaged tissue, dermal filler gels come as a smooth injectable gel placed below the skin's surface to literally 'fill in' or 'plump up' static facial wrinkles and folds that are present at rest, creating a natural and more refreshed facial appearance.

Conventional skin fillers suffer from rapid degradation, require re-injection, and may cause complications with blood flow to the skin. Formulations that promote the regeneration of skin, such as hyaluronic acid cryogel, are highly customizable and can restore the original shape and produce a desirable volume effect on the skin.

# Future Perspectives

The use of cryogels can potentially change the way plastic surgeons treat skin sculpting and soft tissue regeneration by offering a non-toxic, durable, and minimally invasive treatment option for facial rejuvenation and soft tissue regeneration. In the following years, we can expect to see syringes full of this hydrogel included in first-aid boxes, empowering people with the ability to treat wounds in the comfort of their homes. 

Moreover, regenerative gel compositions can be potentially added as an enhancement to topical skincare products. Examples range from moisturizers to further improve their regeneration effect associated with repairing dehydrated and ruptured deeper skin-layers, restoring facial skin areas that are damaged due to popped acne, eczema, or other skin diseases with the support of other antimicrobial ingredient combinations, and restoring micro-cuts or micro-ruptures on the skin surface caused by UV radiation and other skin exposure effects associated to the climate.

Conventional skin fillers suffer from rapid degradation, require re-injection, and may cause complications with blood flow to the skin. Formulations that promote the regeneration of skin, such as hyaluronic acid cryogel, are highly customizable and can restore the original shape and produce a desirable volume effect on the skin.

Future Perspectives

The use of cryogels can potentially change the way plastic surgeons treat skin sculpting and soft tissue regeneration by offering a non-toxic, durable, and minimally invasive treatment option for facial rejuvenation and soft tissue regeneration. In the following years, we can expect to see syringes full of this hydrogel included in first-aid boxes, empowering people with the ability to treat wounds in the comfort of their homes.

Moreover, regenerative gel compositions can be potentially added as an enhancement to topical skincare products. Examples range from moisturizers to further improve their regeneration effect associated with repairing dehydrated and ruptured deeper skin-layers, restoring facial skin areas that are damaged due to popped acne, eczema, or other skin diseases with the support of other antimicrobial ingredient combinations, and restoring micro-cuts or micro-ruptures on the skin surface caused by UV radiation and other skin exposure effects associated to the climate.

description.shortText: An automated flying aid unit mounted with a defibrillator and other life-saving devices, designed to reduce the amount of waiting time for victims and increase their chance of survival.
description.longText:
A drone used to carry medical equipment to speed up the time of rescue and treatment, while also saving resources and fuel with transportation. A GPS guides the drone to the coordinates where a device is providing the current emergency location, thus supplying the necessary support in just a few minutes.

There are many possible uses for an ambulance-like drone. For instance, a drone could be mounted with an automated defibrillator. Upon arrival, emergency personnel can use a video feed to assist the victim and instruct people nearby on how to use the defibrillator properly. It can also be used to deliver organs in an efficient, time-saving manner. This drone has mounted sensors that maintain and monitor the organ, sending information to land in real-time. Its use could go beyond dropping off emergency kits and medicines, undertaking search and rescue missions, or working in zones of natural disasters. It could also be used to collect blood samples, as well as carry units to places where blood loss has occurred. 

This automated flying aid unit helps save lives by expanding existing emergency infrastructure through a network of fast and compact systems capable of providing emergency supplies and establishing a line of communication. An LTE advanced cellphone network infrastructure and cloud-based software may enable the necessary connectivity for controlling data and video, making it possible for the interaction between parties much easier than it currently is.

# Future Perspectives

Possibly, these ambulance drones could extinguish the need for on-land ambulances, thus giving a novel insight into how emergency support would be provided in the future. Medical installations, such as hospitals, would reduce in size once patients could have their medical assistance at the last mile, not only receiving aid when an emergency occurs. Professionals like nurses and doctors could assist patients remotely and also advise, thus avoiding possible emergencies when risk occasions are likely to happen, like in areas under threat.

description.shortText: An urban traffic network of traffic lights powered by sensors, machine vision, and IoT to optimize the flow of vehicles and pedestrians. This technological solution helps solve exacerbated traffic problems, besides preventing possible accidents produced by poorly communicated traffic modes.
description.longText:
Traditional traffic lights combined with sensors, machine vision, and IoT systems, help improve traffic interactions between vehicles and pedestrians. This technological solution helps solve exacerbated traffic problems, besides preventing possible accidents produced by poorly communicated traffic modes.

As IoT progresses to improve the communication between vehicles and traffic signals, this solution optimizes the flow of cars while public transportation becomes more reliable. With the help of machine learning algorithms, the traffic lights would understand traffic volume while it changes in real-time. Bikes and vehicles mounted with GPS and wireless connectivity could send signals to traffic lights, thus warning the system to better plan whenever to shut down a crossroad as the vehicles approach.

Current applications were vulnerable to security-related issues, many of which were often prone to hacking. Weaknesses showed by existing connected traffic lights range from unencrypted wireless connections, default usernames and passwords that can be encountered online, and a debugging port that is exposed to attacks. These issues could be solved by applying intricately encrypted systems, which would make the network more reliable besides refining it to the circumstances of each city it is used.

# Future Perspectives

The use of artificial intelligence to optimize the flow of vehicles and pedestrians has been tested in pilot cities with encouraging initial results, and benefiting cities by reducing CO2 emissions. Together with deep learning, the data gathered from the traffic lights could be used to elaborate predictions of particular zones and design plans to improve urban planning, ranging from expanding lanes to enabling more crosswalks where needed.

Also, in a world with driverless vehicles, the system initially designed for connected traffic lights will be transferred to all other traffic machinery to be interconnected and functioning as a neural system. Autonomous vehicles could transit more fluidly, with no need to hit the breaks. It won't mean just reducing the quantity and intensity of traffic jams; mobility itself would be reimagined, possibly allowing citizens to live farther away from cities, as distances wouldn't affect individual routines.

*Photo/Illustration: monticellllo / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A combination of active agents for a selective mode of protection from urban pollution. It can reduce skin senescence markers, attenuate the expression of UVB damage, and improve skin smoothness with only one topic application.
description.longText:
A combination of active agents, like Dead Sea minerals, for a selective mode of protection from urban pollution. This material can provide complete protection against different types of pollutants, besides being highly beneficial for future antipollution regimens in both pharmaceutical and cosmetic products. 

Also, it is able to reduce skin senescence markers, attenuate the expression of UVB damage, and improve skin smoothness. In addition, other components like Anionic Polysaccharide serve as a physical barrier to the following three types of pollution stresses: atmospheric pollution (carbon particles, PM and heavy metals), domestic pollution (chemicals), and UV radiation, and could also be important for antipollution defense. This product normally comes in the format of a beauty product.

# Future Perspectives

As toxic air continues to envelop major cities worldwide, consumers are becoming increasingly aware of the catastrophic effect this can have on their health, by looking for brands to create new products, services, and environments that can mitigate the impact. To do so, brands need to focus on long-term sustainable solutions that will turn the beauty market into a significant antipollution sector. 

This will potentially result in the wide availability of antipollution-focused cosmetics which combine active agents for a selective mode of protection from various urban pollution factors according to the specific urban environment customers live in. Moreover, due to the growing importance of active antipollution protection, functional antipollution products will potentially arise in other sectors, such as fragrances, allowing antipollution substances to be included in other essential products and become a core part of daily life.

*Photo/illustration: ₢ Nati Melnychuk / unsplash.com*

description.shortText: Artificially intelligent software used for data processing to tackle issues on sustainability, both in terms of natural resource protection and improvement of industrial and agricultural practices.
description.longText:
Technology companies are finding ways to combine the analytical abilities of AI to understand how to enhance their sustainability practices regarding natural systems such as water, forests, transportation, and even wildlife. In combination with precision tools such as satellites and sensors, these programs can analyze all collected data and propose ways humans could identify and make decisions regarding various issues, including suspicious marine traffic, illegal agricultural practices, and other harmful environmental behaviors.

Instead of working as a single application solely reserved for companies, this technology can function as a collective monitoring platform for social and environmental impact by tackling global environmental challenges. For that, AI initiatives are creating open-source tools and APIs to provide models and the base infrastructure for enterprises that want to make their businesses greener and hold themselves more accountable.

It could help the transportation industry elevate its practices by being accountable and making sure the entire fleet is within the low-impact and low-emissions standards. Growing deployment and applications of this technology across different economic and social sectors have the potential to elevate the intelligence with which we manage water resources, understand and deal with varying aspects of pollution across the globe, and integrate different actors for more sustainable practices.

As for wildlife, AI could help save the remaining animal species from extinction by using advanced cloud software to identify these animals and, with the help of deep learning algorithms, monitor programs that can keep an eye on these populations. Also, this technology would support scientists working on wildlife surveys by increasing the efficiency of their tasks. In the case of agriculture, this software could work in conjunction with monitoring systems that could help develop more precise agricultural strategies while providing farming practices with accountability standards.

# Future Perspectives

Considering that all of these tools are available for free, governments and small initiatives could take advantage of this software as a means to pursue accountability and how their practices fit into global objectives in terms of sustainability and global warming. In combination with other technologies and systems such as blockchain and the internet of things, these initiatives could spread in smart cities and add a new layer of sustainable accountability to urban spaces too. Finally, this technology might be able to analyze entire industrial segments, making it easier to create a future of industrial ecology and foster more circular economic practices. This could help companies be viewed as more trustworthy in the eyes of consumers.

*Photo/Illustration:  OSORIOartist / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A geothermal power-recycling plant that extracts CO2 from atmospheric air and transforms the resulting material into a byproduct. Able to generate byproducts, such as concrete, the raw materials produced can be sent to the market, thus establishing a circular carbon economy.
description.longText:
A power-recycling plant that uses geothermal energy to run a mechanism that absorbs CO2 from the atmosphere through a direct-air capture engineering system. This carbon capture technology can extract CO2 already in the atmosphere and collect the harmful gas on a large scale, converting CO2 into byproducts.

By filtering the air that passes over a special liquid, the power plant sticks CO2 into a mixture. The mixture is recycled by releasing the CO2 while using heat. The resulting material is turned into solid carbonate minerals through a high-pressure process that blends carbon dioxide, water, and basalt altogether. Able to generate byproducts, such as concrete, the raw materials produced can be sent to the market. 

# Future Perspectives

The hazards produced by CO2 exposure when transformed into byproducts need to be studied accurately before being marketed. Because it does not necessarily fight fossil fuels, this recycling system may encompass a better temporary alternative than a long-term solution. While countries across the globe prepare to shift to clean energy sources, authorities could create policies that require existing fossil fuel plants to acquire CO2 capturing credits, making it mandatory for the repurposing of the air pollutant gas.

*Photo/Illustration: bannafarsai / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Spherical or treadmill structure mounted with a VR headset that can simulate 360 degrees of continuous movement within a small space, thus providing an immersive experience suitable for training, amusement, and educational uses.
description.longText:
Omnidirectional treadmills (ODTs) are walk-in-place mechanical devices that allow a person to move in any direction, allowing for 360 degrees of movement while using a VR headset. The most common way to achieve this is with a kind of moving floor is a two-axis treadmill that responds in real-time to body movement through trackers such as the headset, and hand and feet-controllers. 

More recent hardware presents wedge-shaped modules or rotatable ball arrays positioned above a traditional linear treadmill for more ergonomic experiences. A novel approach is an omnidirectional sphere, used to simulate more complex movements that involve gravitational rotation like driving and flying while sitting, which use a similar technology under the sphere structure. Also, all of these have safety apparatus such as belts, handrails, or special shoes.

Both of these solutions are being marketed for immersive entertainment applications, such as gaming and location-based entertainment. Nevertheless, this technological solution is expected to be implemented across other industries. In healthcare, this can be used for rehabilitation therapy; in the military, training can be made safer and cheaper. In the architecture industry, engineering and construction would be facilitated while a virtual tour of an upcoming project can take place. Finally, in education, it could be used for immersive teaching experiences, in which students could visit historical sights, for instance.

Due to the price, currently, these omnidirectional bases are used in arcades, events, and large corporations, and they don’t seem to be massively advertised and consumed anytime soon. Yet, as virtual reality designers face a physical hurdle when trying to bring immersive worlds to fruition, this innovative solution holds great expectations. 

# Future Perspectives

This technological solution will likely impact the training and education industries more than any other. It might bring new participants to the surface and possibly democratize its use and applicability. Also, this could catalyze the rise of new high-tech gaming arcades. 

These structures could soon be used to remotely control unmanned vehicles and objects with more precision and live feedback from the field. In the military, armies could be uncrewed while being controlled by a human, possibly located at the army's base or anywhere on earth. This could also disrupt supply-chains with remote drivers and pilots, which would handle duties that would be performed by robots while being protected inside a VR remote treadmill.

description.shortText: Pods that travel inside near-vacuum-sealed pipes using linear induction propulsion systems. It works as an inter-city alternative transportation system for mass transit that could reach cruising speeds of 966 km/h.
description.longText:
A reduced-pressure sealed tube system with a near-zero friction environment for magnetic-levitating pods. These small pods would cruise at 966 km/h, propelled by a linear induction propulsion system allowing passengers to travel long distances in a short amount of time. As its regenerative braking system recovers much of the energy used during deceleration, it would generate more electricity than it consumes, providing the transportation industry and the world with a fresh perspective on clean energy production.

Reduced travel times might fundamentally alter how cities and suburbs are planned and have a disruptive impact on current inter-city transportation systems. Yet, the biggest concern when developing hyperloop projects is the high costs associated with infrastructure. Urban development and human communities must evolve along with the system for the project to be financially viable. This type of transportation solution does not depend solely on the construction and maintenance costs; it must be well-integrated with local economies and broader landscape projects.

# Future Perspectives
This technological solution could alter the way the industrialized world transports cargo. Road freight creates noise pollution, a matter of concern in areas of conservation as well as cities. Replacing a significant share of shipments carried by trucks would create shared value for society. Overall, it offers an attractive shared value proposition, integrating social welfare with economic value in a successful business model.

Concerns regarding safety, costs, and engineering challenges have yet to be fully hashed out, and one of the most challenging issues revolves around regulatory restrictions along with the expensive nature of digging and building underground pipe systems. This advancement for public mobility could also generate friction with companies that rely on old transportation methods; they might be unable or unwilling to adapt to change.

description.shortText: A platform that combines sensors, machine learning, and 3D modeling to simulate, optimize, and monitor groundwater systems. It assists operators in harnessing flood and groundwater flows through wells to automatically update groundwater and surface water levels, with a smaller margin of error.
description.longText:
Due to treatment and exploration methods around the world, natural groundwater cycles are being broken, transforming them into non-renewable resource. Groundwater management tools are combining simulation, sensors, machine learning, and other methods to gather and control data to understand and act on behalf of preservation or diminishing the impact on its recomposing cycles.

Groundwater is a vital global source of water for survival and the livelihoods of many. Many sources are confronted with significant challenges in terms of sustainable management, which will continue to worsen as dependence on water increases with global changes. The problems of our rapidly changing world — not just issues related to global warming but also dealing with future demographic, economic, and political issues — can only be rationally and effectively addressed through collaboration between inter-disciplinary experts and practitioners as well as the affected population.

A real-time cloud-based platform could integrate the software and sensors to automatically update groundwater and surface water levels, with a smaller margin of error. The platform would alert the operator, depending on the scenario, to proactively counteract any issues that might arise. This technology could enable farmers to receive assistance from local or national agriculture and irrigation agencies, including the ability to harness flood flows, and groundwater flows through wells.

# Future Perspectives
With rivers around the world already being exploited at maximum capacity and groundwater systems at risk of contamination, we have tumbled into an era in which multiple simultaneous stresses will drive improved water management to avoid possible severe consequences. Water management systems could simulate complex “what-if” scenarios by predicting human behavior using multi-agent modeling techniques. Understanding the intricate interplay between water systems and social activities is essential if groundwater resources are to be produced sustainably, or otherwise managed to reduce short‐term problems.

If accelerated by the evolution and integration of different types of sensors, IoT, artificial intelligence for monitoring, and biotechnology for microbiological analysis, the combination of groundwater analysis systems would become increasingly viable for their application and large-scale integration.

description.shortText: A miniature projector mounted on glasses that project holographic images directly onto the user's retina, creating an interactive mixed reality layer. This technology could augment daily tasks and educational content with extra data and insights.
description.longText:
Also known as Virtual Retinal Display (VRD) or Retinal Scan Display (RSD), this is a miniature projector mounted on Mixed Reality (MR) glasses that projects a localized light field directly onto the user’s retina. This technological solution creates an interactive mixed reality layer, with virtual 3D objects appearing to float in front of the user, similar to a holographic image, and blends digital content seamlessly with the physical world. 

The MR glasses are lensless, and the tiny projectors are not placed in front of the eyes. The result is a screenless display, which might also present a larger Field of View (FOV) than Near-Eye Display (NED) technologies. This solution might also solve the challenges of current Augmented Reality (AR) glasses that have more complex optical systems, combiners, and bulky designs. 

Current models present higher resolution and excellent color gamut and brightness, making it possible to use in any kind of setting, indoors or outdoors. New models include real-time pupil trackers, which could help improve Field of Depth adjustment by blurring the image that is not in focus. 

The idea of projecting photons directly into someone’s retina may raise some health concerns. By exposing the eye's retina to constant light stimuli, the fluids of the eye tend to dry up, and this increases the risk of eye infection. Also, there is no one-size-fits-all; the projectors must be adequate ergonomically to the users' eye anatomy. 

# Future Perspectives

As this technology becomes more affordable and smaller, it may be the tool to bring mixed reality into the daily lives of many people due to its possibility of a slimmer design. Applications range from industrial production settings where workers can augment their daily tasks with extra data and insights, but also in educational environments where teachers and students can access any layer of augmented and mixed personal data.

*Photo / Illustration: © TimeStopper / adobe.stock.com*
description.longTextHtml:
Also known as Virtual Retinal Display (VRD) or Retinal Scan Display (RSD), this is a miniature projector mounted on Mixed Reality (MR) glasses that projects a localized light field directly onto the user’s retina. This technological solution creates an interactive mixed reality layer, with virtual 3D objects appearing to float in front of the user, similar to a holographic image, and blends digital content seamlessly with the physical world.

The MR glasses are lensless, and the tiny projectors are not placed in front of the eyes. The result is a screenless display, which might also present a larger Field of View (FOV) than Near-Eye Display (NED) technologies. This solution might also solve the challenges of current Augmented Reality (AR) glasses that have more complex optical systems, combiners, and bulky designs.

Current models present higher resolution and excellent color gamut and brightness, making it possible to use in any kind of setting, indoors or outdoors. New models include real-time pupil trackers, which could help improve Field of Depth adjustment by blurring the image that is not in focus.

The idea of projecting photons directly into someone’s retina may raise some health concerns. By exposing the eye's retina to constant light stimuli, the fluids of the eye tend to dry up, and this increases the risk of eye infection. Also, there is no one-size-fits-all; the projectors must be adequate ergonomically to the users' eye anatomy.

Future Perspectives

As this technology becomes more affordable and smaller, it may be the tool to bring mixed reality into the daily lives of many people due to its possibility of a slimmer design. Applications range from industrial production settings where workers can augment their daily tasks with extra data and insights, but also in educational environments where teachers and students can access any layer of augmented and mixed personal data.

description.shortText: A person's unique brainwave pattern used to create a distinctive, unhackable, and uncopiable signature. It would allow users to make payments and other transactions, while significantly improving safety and efficiency.
description.longText:
With the advancement of hacking methods, concerns about the privacy and safety of our data continue to grow ever more critical. One way to avoid identity theft could be to use your brainwave patterns as a signature. Brainwaves are unique to each person, and, for the time being, cannot be hacked or copied, and since brainwaves are intangible, they cannot be physically stolen either.

By detecting a person's brainwaves through a receptor device, the signals of the brain activity would be identified and patterned. This technology could be used to grant access to particular places, by opening doors as the user approaches, or as a personal authentication system or a "passthought." Every time the user thinks about a chosen word, image, or memory, it would reproduce a pattern of recognizable brainwaves, enough to grant access to websites, ATMs, or stores. It would allow users to make payments and other transactions, while significantly improving safety and efficiency.

One potential concern is that brainwave systems fail to recognize users when they show unusual brain states, such as stress or fatigue. It seems as though these forms of mental distress provoke irregular brainwaves, and detection devices fail to register the correct user due to the continually shifting signals sent by the brain itself. To avoid these situations, machine-learning algorithms could be deployed into a particular device and trained to recognize an individual's unique brainwave frequency across a variety of moods.

Studies show that mental-health disturbances, such as depression or anxiety, can be measured and identified through brainwaves. We could envision a job interview in which the interviewer measures the candidate's brainwaves, (with or without explicit consent) and uses this data to corroborate their final decision. Despite the opportunities for accessing this type of data, ethical and moral concerns should be set across the board for this technology to be deployed. Researchers need to investigate the point at which brainwaves cannot be detected to guarantee the users' privacy.  

# Future Perspectives 

Brainwave measurement is one of the most resilient forms of identification. Since brainwave data is currently impossible to clone or duplicate, a worldwide brainwave signature databank could be created. In this scenario, it would be easy to instantly identify any given person without the need for consent from the target individual. Ultimately, it would lead to a world without the possibility of lies or deceit, where personal identity and personal choices could be accessed continuously at will by those in power.

*Photo / Illustration: © Gorodenkoff / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Underwater pods designed to cultivate seaweed and other marine species by taking advantage of all the characteristics found in seawater, such as constant temperature and protection from exposure to land-based extreme weather conditions.
description.longText:
Farming aquatic flora and fauna offshore in the open ocean could be a more sustainable approach to feed a growing world population with low environmental impacts. Different from underground hydroponic pods that depend on cooling and heating systems to regulate the temperature, underwater farms offer a more stable environment to yield crops. Underwater pods are usually submerged five to eight meters below the surface, providing a steady temperature to culture, while avoiding exposure to land-based extreme weather conditions.

While lettuce, basil, and strawberries are plants already grown in underwater farms, other approaches include cultivating seafood such as scallops, clams, oysters, and mussels in water columns alongside seaweed and shellfish. As opposed to regular crops, these ocean farming systems remove nitrogen, phosphorus, and carbon dioxide from the water, thus helping protect ocean ecosystems and decrease ocean acidification, which is a consequence of carbon pollution. By soaking up carbon and keeping surrounding waters safe for shellfish and other vulnerable creatures, these seaweed-populated underwater farms would serve as a kind of sanctuary for crabs, shrimp, and other marine species.

Restorative ocean farming could play a vital role in helping coastal communities and the planet's climate. However, specific environmental concerns relating to the use of pesticides to prevent diseases are rising accordingly. Solutions such as nanobiopesticides are relatively promising, even though studies never made into testing it yet. 

# Future Perspectives

Although most of the features used in these underwater farms are specifically related to seawater and its geographical features, the same idea could be applied to rivers and lakes as well. This approach is another solution for famine and reduces the amount of land occupied for farming animal protein and food for humans. Nevertheless, freshwater conditions – such as flora and fauna – are different from the sea, so adaptations on structure and practices are expected.

Other questions that emerge include geopolitical issues such as where these pods would be positioned offshore, raising concerns on how to establish appropriate border policies for this technology to be correctly deployed.

*Photo/Illustration: Zstock / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: An injectable "in-body GPS" that diagnoses and guide drug administration to certain parts of the body. It communicates by either sending a wireless signal or alert to an external device or by performing a programmable action.
description.longText:
An injectable "in-body GPS" that diagnoses and guide drug administration to certain parts of the body. The device internally monitors physical or molecular properties from within the body of a human or animal for medical purposes. Some implants may generate a controlled response, done remotely through wireless signals or programmed into the implant when it meets specific criteria. Responses may include managed drug release capabilities, biomarkers, or inflammation sensors to monitor the bloodstream. Other possibly of collected data may consist of protein content, cholesterol and pharmaceuticals.

These implantable sensors can also continuously monitor physical data such as respiratory rate, heartbeat, or blood pressure. They could also improve the monitoring of chronic diseases, such as Parkinson’s and certain types of cancer, helping provide early care. Potentially, they can monitor the physical performance of athletes, astronauts, soldiers and individuals that need closer attention. Defibrillators, pacemakers, and artificial joints are possible medical applications for these markers.

The majority of available devices are transdermal, given the low risk and easy application. At the same time, these types of sensors also raise concerns over data privacy. They could potentially be used as a tool for manipulation and control in authoritarian governments, as a way to define the price of health insurance, or even as a potential source of human guidance by the companies that gather the actual data. Additionally, companies could also collect and sell sensitive data to third parties to enhance their services and personalize their practices according to the personal details of users. In order to avoid violating user privacy, proper protocols need to be defined regarding the use and management of these devices upon their deployment.

# Future Perspectives

There is still some fine-tuning to be done in these implants, like reducing the size to millimeters instead of centimeters. Also, wireless signals could bounce off many parts of a human body —and are significantly more powerful, reflecting off the skin than on any implantable markers. For this reason, small semiconductors that help set different signals apart are being tested. Self-healing and self-powered implants are also improvements under study. The goal is to finally make patient care that's less expensive, invasive and time-consuming than has previously been possible.

By dynamically measuring the physical states of the user and cross-referencing this data with exercise graphics, activities, attention span, and even internet browsing activity, a sensor could generate a holistic quantified view of the individual. Paired with an AI assistant, this could help individuals navigate life decisions based on the actual data archive and physical reactions, accessible from an application. This data could be easily accessed and shared with a doctor if necessary. On the other hand, if this type of device were to be hacked, or the data otherwise compromised and provided to third parties, an enormous amount of power would be generated, especially over individuals.

*Photo / Illustration: © Microgen / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Biochar is a supplement fertilizer with soil carbon sequestration capabilities. It helps decrease water requirements by 25-30% and chemical fertilizer requirements by 25-50%.
description.longText:
Through a process called pyrolysis, charcoal is produced by burning biomass, such as wood, crop wastes, solid organic residues, fecal sludge, or manure, while cutting off the supply of oxygen. A recent study found that biochar has the potential to sequester up to 4.8bn tons of carbon dioxide per year.

The carbon in the resulting biochar is very slow to break down. This means the carbon biomass absorbed from the atmosphere is locked up for — potentially — hundreds or even thousands of years. As such, the capacity to store nutrients and promote plant growth comes down to a super-thin but sophisticated organic coating created on both the outer and inner surfaces of its particles as they compost in the soil.

Making and using biochar can serve several purposes in addition to sequestering carbon and can be used in home gardens, city parks, sports fields, reforestation, and small and large-scale agriculture. Adding it to soils can improve its fertility — acting as a slow-release sponge for water and nutrients — and boost crop yields. Additionally, adding biochar makes the ground darker, reducing its albedo, meaning the land will absorb more of the sun’s energy and warm more rapidly; it also can prevent soil erosion.

In addition, recent studies showed that biochar is an excellent solution for replenishing soil depleted by mining and other activities, since new fragile seeds thrive in that type of soil, becoming an essential tool in reforestation efforts.

# Future Perspectives

Due to the variety of potential uses for biochar, researchers believe that applications will significantly increase in the future. Ongoing monitoring research for the use of biochar in Finland has pointed to a possible strong future position in the gardening and green building sectors — more specifically, the areas of composting, green roofs, seedbeds, filtering, and managing stormwater, and urban runoff.

description.shortText: An online-mapping platform that geographically pinpoints and stores where criminal activity is occurring in real-time. The map is available to the public and would also be useful for law enforcement analysis.
description.longText:
An online map updated in real-time with data involving areas where criminal activity has occurred. A webpage platform hosts this online map, and it is available to the public as a free tool. It serves both as a platform to display the records of areas where instances of crimes happen most, and as an analytical tool to examine incident patterns such as assault, robbery, sex crimes, vehicle theft, among others.

This model uses an advanced mapping engine to cover large areas of geographical territory, and it is connected to police bodies databases that continuously feed the platform with accurate data regarding recent criminal cases and include the area where they occurred. The crime-mapping platform is responsible for delivering valuable and free information over crime rates in neighborhoods and cities, besides being an accessible interface to the latest reports from local law enforcement agencies.

Besides checking recent crime activities around areas, citizens can also sign up to receive automated mailings reports about criminal activities in their neighborhoods. It enables more in-depth crime prevention and offers tools not only to better fight crime but to address community-oriented measures. 

# Future Perspectives

By performing an efficient crime analysis, law agencies could mitigate crime, improve operations, while making more accurate data-driven decisions. Civilians could also use such tools to become more aware of their communities. By getting a bigger picture of their surroundings, it would provide a precise view of when and where law enforcement activities happened, and to address solutions later to tackle why they happened.

*Photo/Illustration: kovop58 / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Predictive analytics integrated with geographical data that analyzes past and present communication channels of social media posts to predict possible areas that are prone to conflicts. It identifies where it would be better to intervene, and what level of intervention will be necessary.
description.longText:
Predictive analytics integrated with geographical data that analyzes past and present communication from social media channels to predict possible areas that are prone to conflicts. It identifies where it would be better to intervene, and what level of intervention will be necessary. Besides having access to criminal records from groups that were already targeted for illegal activity, quantitative conflict models also focus on analyzing past and present financial transactions and data extracted from crowdsourced platforms. 

Apart from analyzing communication patterns, conflict prediction models incorporate geographical information to automate the identification of possible conflict areas. These models can be scaled to identify risk areas in an entire region or within a city. By using algorithms that forecast risks, similar to predicting policing needs and extreme weather changes, trouble spots could be flagged. 

The patterns in violence and the underlying causes and relations are shifting rapidly, making the process of modeling predictive systems more intricate when it comes to conflict analytics. Due to the structural complexity surrounding processes of peace and conflict, predictive models are still in their infancy. With the help of machine learning, early warning systems could be created to help the global community to take action before violent breakouts. 
Regarding online criminal organizations, governments could more efficiently carry out attacks just by analyzing the formation of online group interactions, thus enabling authorities to act upon them —either preemptively or defensively.


# Future Perspectives

When models are able to predict conflict accurately, they should be able to provide information on where it is best to intervene and ideally give suggestions of how much intervention will be necessary for a peaceful outcome. For a conflict to happen, there are intangible factors that are crucial for predicting when an event is about to occur. The willingness to fight, the weapons used, the funding from sources outside the country, besides the changes in political ideology, are some intangibles that should be seriously taken into account when adding data to predictive analytics. Since the success of predictive models depends directly on the quality and availability of data, global cooperation will be necessary to create databases that can be used to feed algorithms. 

Advances in the field of deep learning that allow real-time sentiment analysis of text, audio, and even video are providing new data-driven indicators that could be integrated with spatial prediction models. Advances in machine reasoning could allow future conflict models to do more than make predictions: they could potentially offer explanations for violence and strategies for preventing it.

*Photo/Illustration: Alexander / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: This chip-sized device mimics the dynamics of a living organ for safe and efficient tests and improves the physiology of in-vitro models. It enables more efficient research approaches in the fields of biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and chemicals.
description.longText:
More important than a simple issue of economics, the testing of products and pharmaceuticals is ethically problematic considering the animal rights abuses and dangers of using human subjects for testing with unknown consequences. In an attempt to combat these challenges, scientists have developed a chip-sized device that can mimic a living organ and its dynamics on a tiny scale.

This device, popularly known as organ-on-a-chip, contains cells layered in the hollow compartments of the chip according to the actual, emulated organ; fluid flow (blood and lymph) is reproduced via channels. It produces normal levels of organ functionality, allowing an analysis of biochemical, genetic, and metabolic activities. Connecting chips could help systematically map the functions and interactions of the whole body while proving that living organs are more predictable than expected and assist in understanding how diseases develop and progress accordingly.

An organ-on-a-chip can enable new, more efficient biomedical research approaches, more reliably producing results when predicting the effects on humans. It can accelerate research and discoveries in the fields of biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and chemicals. At the same time, academic institutions and hospitals can also benefit from this technology to develop and test personalized medicine. However, the challenge is to make this device as accurate as possible to replicate the simulated results in the real world.

# Future Perspectives

The large-scale adoption of organs-on-a-chip could reduce the time necessary to develop new drugs. It creates more room for experimenting with innovative formulas while abiding by ethical codes throughout the world. Animal and human testing could become something of the past while maintaining industry efficiency.

As the technology matures, these chips could be available as point-of-care testing. That is, at the time and place of patient care, especially in critical care settings such as the intensive care units, the operating room, and the emergency department. 

Eventually, such chips could be made on a personalized scale. Every single person could have their own set of chips, with each of them representing a particular organ. Enter personalized tests: drugs and cosmetics could be first tested on the chip to check for incompatibilities and potential reactions, and only applied directly to the organism following satisfactory results. Unintended consequences, which create health issues and general frustration with personal care products, could be significantly reduced. Finally, the ultimate goal of organ-on-a-chip technology might be integrating numerous organs into a single chip. From this moment onwards, it would be possible to build a more complex multi-organ chip model, finally achieving a “human-on-a-chip” aspiration.

description.shortText: A hybrid model of currency built on both crypto and fiat assets. It is based on a third-generation blockchain using a delegated proof of stake consensus mechanism that provides methods for validating blocks and transactions for governance functions for the common public good.
description.longText:
A hybrid model of currency built on both crypto and fiat assets. It is based on a third-generation blockchain using a delegated proof of stake consensus mechanism that provides ways of validating blocks and transactions for governance functions for the common public good. 

Like all resources, money cannot be limitlessly exploited, even in a digital format. For many, cryptocurrencies are seen as a way to bring more fairness to the global economic system. Yet, due to their decentralized nature, there is no clear central ownership and stabilization management, thus in past years, their price volatility has jeopardized their potential. Large tech companies are on their way to issuing digital currencies backed by some 'real-world' assets as a collective intent to solve this issue, but this movement also raises concerns that private entities may tend to act in their own interests. 

In order to create a more trustworthy and sustainable economic system, governments around the world are trying to partner with private actors to issue hybrid coins with legal tender status. Through this model, crypto-fiat currencies attract a broader network participation the more significant the chain. Besides connecting distant economic systems, the purpose is to promote long-term sustainability and prevent runaway inflation, by algorithmically fixing the annual increase rate on the blockchain. To ensure fairness, each supply grown is automatically sent to all eligible users - not to the banking system as in traditional finance.

Sovereign cryptocurrency rules of issuance are embedded into the protocol, algorithmically enforced apps and DAOs deployed on the blockchain as well. By legitimizing cryptocurrencies, funds are made available to law enforcement. Additionally, in the third-generation blockchain, the consensus is achieved through less energy usage than in proof-of-work and other similar mechanisms. Furthermore, there is no particular class of nodes required in this protocol, like the miners in the blockchain ecosystem. By providing quick finality, low latency, open participation, with a green, mining-less, and sustainable environmental impact, sovereign cryptocurrency could also contribute to the UN Sustainability Goals. 

# Future Perspectives

In the next decade, the development of the Internet of Things (IoT) across the globe may require viable economic assets capable of bridging the gap of the digital and physical world. Hybrid models of currency might be vital for transforming a more significant part of the population into autonomous economic actors, all by all connecting the IoT capabilities with individuals with regular civil duties such as tax payments, insurances, and licensing fees. The digital economy would turn into a synthetic model, facilitating the regulation of marginalized markets, and enhancing peer-to-peer transactions through a collaborative regulatory framework.

description.longText:
The use of virtual reality to train teams throughout various industries, creating virtual environments that simulate real-life situations without the associated risks, as a means to enhance and complement real-world exploration, could provide a solid education. 

Since early education is all about learning through experience, immersive 360º environments can engage even the youngest students and stimulate them in an environment in which they can interact with objects. From military to medical, industrial, and service-based industries, virtual reality provides a new way to learn mechanical and even interpersonal tasks while reducing accidents and increasing worker efficiency and proficiency.

# Future Perspectives

Graduate students in the fields of engineering, architecture and design, medicine and life sciences can benefit from virtual reality training while simulating applications, surgeries and medical procedures in a virtual environment. On the other hand, when applied to schools, it could emulate a virtual classroom or present new settings and time periods for teaching biology and history.

description.shortText: Blockchain-based service that anonymously secures and stores an online distributed proof-of-existence for any document. It creates a 'digital fingerprint' that is easily traceable while also adding a layer of security in proving data ownership without revealing the actual data.
description.longText:
A blockchain-based service that anonymously secures and stores an online distributed proof-of-existence for any document, as well as proof-of-ownership and document ownership transfer. While not serving as document storage, documents and files are time-stamped and assigned a digital fingerprint within the blockchain to prevent unauthorized tampering and modification. It allows a public verification of the document’s date, authenticity, origin, integrity, and content without publicly disclosing the content itself. Biometric identification, such as fingerprints, could be used as a digital signature (or private key in cryptography terms) to prove that an individual owns a particular document.  

Traditional centralized entities that secure information and authenticity, such as banks, could replace their current systems with blockchain notaries, giving the digital hash the same status as legal validation. Instead of physically visiting registry offices to validate information, all verifications could be done online. This service could add additional security for digital transactions on the internet, thus allowing extensive cooperation.

The implementation of this protocol creates a "digital footprint" that is easily traceable, adding a layer of security that proves data ownership without revealing the data itself. Considering the advantages, government agencies and public services could employ a distributed network accompanied by a public ledger instead of central notary authorities.

# Future Perspectives

Birth and marriage certificates could also be issued using blockchain notaries, reducing the cost and time and improving safety. This could guarantee the right to identity for children when they are born or even recognize same-sex marriage in places where it is still not legalized.

One possible method of using blockchain notaries is developing smart contracts that invoke a statutory durable power of attorney when the owner/user is not available or disabled. This process would alleviate crucial problems that affect people with mobility limitations. By learning the decision-making methodologies through machine learning, this technology could automate the whole certification system. Questions regarding the level of trust state governments would give to the blockchain remain uncertain, especially considering its by-design resistance to allow any modification made by a central authority on the data.

description.shortText: Software fed with data from sensors distributed in water pipelines able to record leaks in treatment plants and water distribution systems. It continuously supplies operators with information about the status of the water pipelines, avoiding losses, and providing an accurate basis for action.
description.longText:
Although large urban centers often make massive investments in the construction and maintenance of underground pipes, leaks of different sizes and scales still represent a constant drain on natural and economic resources. Large networks, related to numerous other systems, of underground pipes that are often old or refurbished, make it even more complex to monitor, detect, and correct leaks.

One of the measures taken to minimize water mismanagement impacts is the development and broad application of interconnected and decentralized pipe monitoring and management solutions. Specifically developed for the detection and correction of leaks in water networks, these systems can control tasks and carry out standard processes. They combine digital systems that record both sizeable and small-but-growing leaks in treatment plants and distribution systems.

Based on thermal imaging, remote sensors, and controllers - such as in the case of force valves that measure the radial pressure gradient of leaks - these input/output units are essential in gathering specific, and on-time information and data about leaks. The data collected from sensors range from current leaks, with their precise location, and ones that could happen shortly. This IoT software-based solution expands the capability of the people responsible for maintaining the distribution network, guaranteeing adequate and decisive actions to prevent a higher volume of water loss.

# Future Perspectives

The integration of pipeline intelligence is already a reality in cities around the world, but the complexity of the technologies used, and high-operational costs limit wider use. Current efforts for technological development and deployment must sit in tandem with the current coming technologies to enable these systems to be adopted and integrated, improving system accuracy, and decreasing the cost of implementation. Large-scale use of government homologated systems should be encouraged as an effective way to save natural and financial resources. With prominent advancements in robotic integration, leaks could be autonomously repaired, even eliminate the amount of time taken for a human to see and respond to the issue.

description.shortText: Augmented Reality (AR) models applied at workforce environments allowing professionals to interact with 1:1 scale 3D models of spaces, and pieces of materials in real-time.
description.longText:
Able to be implemented in almost any industry, the technological innovations provided by AR enable the incorporation of virtual elements into real environments. By overlaying a physical space with virtual data and 1:1 scale holograms, the user could spot onsite problems, increase accuracy, and avoid costly mistakes. Through smartphones and smart-glasses, it could contain a range of specific sensors, such as infrared cameras and infrared light projectors, allowing it to measure depth and project 3D imagery successfully. Also, a thermal camera could overlay thermal measurements on the visual display, helping spot abnormalities. 

As augmented reality solutions can provide a combination of virtual architectural designs with the physical surroundings, it could perhaps make site experts become remote experts. The AR goggles can allow experts to remotely visualize what the user sees on-site while providing an interface through which experts could virtually modify/update the asset themselves or give the user instructions on how to execute the procedure on their own. 

This technological solution helps lower maintenance costs and machinery downtime through quick component substitution, identification, and new connection set-up. Another example of use could be in equipment monitoring. In work sites where hundreds of different machines move about, AR can help workers recognize these machines' locations faster. Finally, in underground construction, it could allow users to view unseeable things, such as hidden underground trenches or buried cables. 

# Future Perspectives

Concerning the planning stages of construction, AR is expected to become one of the most common methods to showcase projects to clients, ensuring their requirements have been addressed prior to construction. Also, as AR could refine the education, planning, safety, and efficiency of workers, it may help avoid incidents and flaws. Every year, many construction workers die due to accidents at construction sites. Training and enabling them to have a better view of their surroundings could prevent them from having accidents that could even lead to death.

description.shortText: Analytical predictive models that data-mine criminal databases to identify possible offenders, the location of future crime scenes, and predict trends in illicit activities.
description.longText:
By data-mining criminal databases, social media, and surveillance devices, predictive analytics can support police bodies in identifying possible offenders, trends in illegal activity, and even the locations of future crime scenes. The automated combination of statistical studies and AI assesses pre-established parameters and determines the probability of a given citizen of committing a crime or even becoming a victim of modern-day slavery, for example. By flagging individuals who are likely to become criminals or repeat certain illegal activities, the system could intervene with preventive action, such as counseling or community management programs to avoid potentially harmful behaviors.

The use of predictive policing is part of a continuous historical shift from reactive to proactive policing. By using data-driven software to map hotbeds of criminal activity, police departments can develop real-time intelligence to make better use of their workforce, saving both human and economic resources. Apart from improving the effectiveness of law enforcement, algorithms could also potentially reduce bias in the arrest patterns of minorities and specific ethnic groups. 

Conversely, predictive algorithms could reinforce discrimination, directing police patrols to target minorities disproportionately. Predictive analytics are based on the data that is fed into the algorithmic structure. Areas with high crime rates that receive more policing and communities in which more arrests occur, could lead these predictive analytics to reflect inherent biases instead of analyzing a crime based on the current facts and singular aspects of the event. Frequently, machine learning models are unable to explain how they produce their results, and the concept of reasonable suspicion could be difficult to enforce legally. Whereas historically, a police officer would be expected to justify their decisions. Therefore, the allocation of police enforcement resources using a computer shifts the accountability from people to machines and circuitry. 

# Future Perspectives

While predictive analytics offers an immense number of opportunities, implementation requires the use of open and publicly auditable systems. Initially, this technological solution could function more like an aid for lawyers, public defenders, and police officers than a standalone system. In a culture where many fundamental parts of society are being reorganized through computational techniques, human-based ethical governance of these solutions becomes increasingly important. 

If algorithms are fed with diverse data extracted from different types of social and cultural aspects, it could probably avoid predictions that lead to unfair outcomes, such as discrimination against skin color, social class, or sexual orientation. It would reduce possible collateral damaged of these digital analytics platforms on both fundamental rights and public trust.

description.shortText: Driverless buses that operate within standard traffic conditions and patterns predetermined for most bus routes. Overall, they hold the potential to improve traffic conditions and commuting since they would communicate with traffic lights to cross junctions and automatically stop at stations.
description.longText:
One of modern society's biggest challenges is public transportation, which desperately needs to be overhauled in order to benefit the whole community. In terms of efficiency in comparison to self-driving cars, self-driving shuttles and buses have the potential to significantly improve traffic conditions and commuting because they manage to move a large number of people at once. At the same time, they would also change the way users experience the mobility, as there would not be a driver onboard the vehicle.

The main highlights for this concept include the possibility for the bus or shuttle to drive itself along suitable routes, communicate with traffic lights to cross junctions, and automatically stop at stations. They would also need more sophisticated technology to operate since they might need to follow pre-programmed routes based on the specialized demand of municipal public transit systems and operate within the dense urban traffic conditions and patterns that usually come along with most bus routes.

# Future Perspectives

By using the information and data gathered by these self-driving vehicles, bus/shuttle services could change their routes more dynamically. They could meet people's transportation needs more efficiently by leveraging their traffic routes according to user needs. The use and analysis of urban geographical data, coupled with information coming from individual users, would help identify new passenger behavior, making it easier to design routes that are not being serviced by publicly operated transport.

description.shortText: A wearable standalone device that allows different degrees of immersive reality experiences, from wholly inserted in a virtual space to digital content overlaying the physical world.
description.longText:
Computer glasses that function as a standalone wearable device that is able to provide audiovisual experiences through the combination of physical-and-virtual environments. The glasses stimulate human senses, triggering the brain to feel immersed in simulations that play with the human perception of reality. 

The XR glasses can encompass experiences ranging from Augmented Reality (AR), Mixed Reality (MR), and VR (Virtual Reality). To create immersive digital content, the glasses are mounted with electronic varifocal, dynamic lenses, and Near-Eye Displays, enabling different degrees of extended reality experiences, including virtual occlusion, which allows for digital objects to intertwine with varying layers of the physical world. Current developments are integrating next-generation SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping), environment and biometric sensors, and eye-trackers to the glasses. 

XR tools are gaining traction not only in the gaming industry. Medical staff is implementing XR glasses to enhance precision and display anatomic characteristics as well as vital information during surgery or as a therapeutic tool for patients with psychiatric or motor-control conditions. Education, physical workspaces, industrial engineering, and supply-chain, are some other areas impacted by this technology. 

# Future Perspectives

The XR glasses could be mounted with hearables to enhance the experience. Hearables, designed as earbuds or headphones, could provide surround 8D sound to function as a trigger to interact with digital content in an immersive experience. 

In the future, XR tools can evolve from on-body gadgets to become in-body implants that are automatically linked to the functions of organic bodies. New developments in implantables are likely to change the way people experience digital content and virtual spaces without the need to access said content by wearing gadgets. The transhumanist movement, for instance, looks into the possibility of merging man and machine by putting these devices directly inside the human body, thus incorporating and fusing technology with biology.

description.shortText: A wearable machine that enhances human movement to perform repetitive motions or carry heavy objects. Powered by a system of electric motors, pneumatics, levers, and hydraulics, an exoskeleton allows limb movement with increased precision, strength, and endurance.
description.longText:
Powered by a system of electric motors, pneumatics, levers, and hydraulics, this wearable mobile machine allows limb movement while increasing strength and endurance. Exoskeletons are used to compensate for physical and motor deficiencies or aid humans when doing heavy work.

There are two categories of exoskeletons devices: active and passive. The active exoskeletons require motors to aid the user, and passive ones use artificial muscles and springs to store the energy put out by the user's body movement. New exoskeletons are starting to use softer materials and active clothes, avoiding metal frames and increasing freedom of movement for the wearer.

People that perform repetitive motions or carry heavy objects, such as in manufacturing, construction, agriculture, could use this assistive device when performing hazardous tasks to boost productivity and decrease muscular tension. In military applications and rescue operations, this technology could improve mobility and engagement capabilities for soldiers or firefighters on the ground, thus enhancing their effectiveness and reducing mortality.

In the healthcare industry, for instance, exoskeletons could be used for rehabilitation or mobility issues. People with neuromuscular diseases, such as Ehlers–Danlos syndromes (EDS), or even the elderly, could take advantage of this device by mimicking human movement more accurately and maximizing patient effort by providing a rigorous, targeted therapy session. In such cases, the human control of locomotion modes can be inconvenient and cognitively demanding. Therefore, to maximize the benefits of exoskeletons assistance,  computer vision and deep learning recognition systems may support the development of automated locomotion techniques to predict different walking environments and adapt between different locomotion modes accordingly.

In gaming, exoskeletons are emerging as commercial devices to exert an opposite and reactive force on the user while using a virtual reality headset. This feature could provide, for instance, the appropriate resistance to make the user feel they are walking, swimming, or carrying heavy objects virtually.

# Future Perspectives

Exoskeletons or power-assisted suits could become an essential part of all industries that require manual labor. As soft exo-tech becomes more affordable, it could lead to mass-produced personal mobility machines for everyone. These fashionable, high-tech devices would enable independence, improve overall physical well-being, and be recognized as a status symbol, like a car in modern society.

Data collected from humans or even animals equipped with exoskeletons could be used to train an artificially intelligent system that ultimately carries out tasks without the need for a human or animal operator. When coupled with machine-learning algorithms, it could calculate the proper amount of motor assistance to deliver additional resistance to the user at any given moment. The suit could also be tailor-fitted, adjusted to fit the exact needs of each user —from an elderly couple going on a stroll to a firefighter sprinting into a burning building.

Although most of today's solutions work by amplifying muscle movement and use force for haptic feedback, advancements in neuroprosthetics and brain-machine interfaces could soon make it possible to control an exoskeleton directly with thought. Current research efforts show that readings from attached sensors could be fed back to the brain, creating a sensation that the exoskeleton is not a separate entity but part of the body and mind. In other words, designers could extend the nervous system into powerful exoskeletons that humans control and feel with their thoughts.

People with neuromuscular diseases, such as Ehlers–Danlos syndromes (EDS), or even the elderly, could take advantage of this device by mimicking human movement more accurately and maximizing patient effort by providing a rigorous, targeted therapy session. In such cases, the human control of locomotion modes can be inconvenient and cognitively demanding. Therefore, to maximize the benefits of exoskeletons assistance, computer vision and deep learning recognition systems may support the development of automated locomotion techniques to predict different walking environments and adapt between different locomotion modes accordingly.

In gaming, exoskeletons are emerging as commercial devices to exert an opposite and reactive force on the user while using a virtual reality headset. This feature could provide, for instance, the appropriate resistance to make the user feel they are walking, swimming, or carrying heavy objects virtually.

Future Perspectives

Exoskeletons or power-assisted suits could become an essential part of all industries that require manual labor. As soft exo-tech becomes more affordable, it could lead to mass-produced personal mobility machines for everyone. These fashionable, high-tech devices would enable independence, improve overall physical well-being, and be recognized as a status symbol, like a car in modern society.

Data collected from humans or even animals equipped with exoskeletons could be used to train an artificially intelligent system that ultimately carries out tasks without the need for a human or animal operator. When coupled with machine-learning algorithms, it could calculate the proper amount of motor assistance to deliver additional resistance to the user at any given moment. The suit could also be tailor-fitted, adjusted to fit the exact needs of each user —from an elderly couple going on a stroll to a firefighter sprinting into a burning building.

Although most of today's solutions work by amplifying muscle movement and use force for haptic feedback, advancements in neuroprosthetics and brain-machine interfaces could soon make it possible to control an exoskeleton directly with thought. Current research efforts show that readings from attached sensors could be fed back to the brain, creating a sensation that the exoskeleton is not a separate entity but part of the body and mind. In other words, designers could extend the nervous system into powerful exoskeletons that humans control and feel with their thoughts.

description.shortText: A credit-tracking system that evaluates and ranks citizen behavior, quantifying it into a social credit code, linked to a permanent and nontransferable record. Records could be accessed by governments and private companies while allowing citizens to evaluate who they want to be associated with.
description.longText:
A set of algorithms that monitor and assess the trustworthiness of individuals.  By collecting data from social media, public databases such as criminal records, and surveillance cameras, it is possible to rate citizens' participation in society. Depending on partnerships with private parties, it might even be possible to collect data from a variety of sources such as e-commerce websites or even bank accounts. This system is generally based on parameters predefined by the authorities in compliance with universal fundamental rights. Records could be accessed by governments and private companies, while also allowing citizens to evaluate who they want to be associated with. 

The different collected data generates a social-credit score that serves as a way to either reward good behavior or penalize citizens with low ratings. If individuals drop below a predefined number of points, they could be denied loans or access to products or services. Penalties could include delaying paperwork, restricting opportunities for work, or reducing internet speeds, among other consequences. By having a good score, one could skip different types bureaucracies and have several advantages among other citizens. A high score could as well be rewarded with acceptance into universities, better job prospects, discounts on utilities, low-interest loans, and even prioritized in public services, such as transport or hospitals. A government partnered with corporations, for instance, could generate “credit scores” by developing a credit reporting system for individuals. 

Regarding environmental issues, this technology could make possible the analyses and rewards of sustainable behaviors through loyalty points and discounts on purchases. The more popular these systems become, the deeper the level of consumer brand engagement. Nevertheless, by turning every person’s experiences into public transactions, it could enhance the polarization of society, increasing competition between citizens who behave according to society's norms and those who do not. 

In the current world, inequality is a burden that most people are struggling with. An evaluation system that takes into account an individual's behavior could become a factor that might increase the already prevailing social divide. A social currency, that evaluates someone's family background and social class but also the choices they take daily, could assume the shape of a prejudice-based system. As a solution, privacy protocols should be taken seriously to ensure this technology is deployed correctly. Otherwise, we might be creating a tool for everyone to silently and secretly monitor each other, thus producing a society without the need for police officers; everyone polices each other. 

# Future Perspectives

By combining distinct ratings with artificial intelligence, social-score programs could have a profound impact on how society behaves both online and offline. Algorithms could autonomously improve themselves by generating their own parameters to define an upstanding citizen accurately. Because these algorithms learn in probabilistic terms, a new type of society could emerge; frowning upon harmful digital behavior. This technological development could either help citizens achieve optimal citizenship scores or lead to ostracism and, ultimately, exile.

Different surveillance systems could immediately flag citizens with low scores, following them more closely than citizens with high scores. Any misbehavior, no matter the severity, would be noted and immediately punished with the help of robot police audits. Finally, instead of exclusively relying on data collected from digital services, live conversations could be scored from microphones scattered across the city.  

These negative aspects could be exacerbated through deep-learning techniques, bringing other complex layers to the subject. In essence, machines embedded with sensors capable of reading people's micro expressions and intentions could rate citizens by their most profound psychological aspects.
