description.shortText: An integrated control system that combines IoT communication devices, flow predictions, and automatic parameter adjustments to remotely control, monitor, and maintain large and complex facilities based on real-time information.
description.longText:
An integrated control system, based on real-time information derived from IoT communication devices, sensors, and flow prediction systems designed to remotely control, monitor, and maintain large and complex facilities and settings. From factories, power plants, network operations centers, airports, farms, to urban areas, it remotely manages all the variables that need to be systematized, such as traffic flow, supply chain logistics, and airport management, among others.   

This monitoring system extracts data from a certain setting through sensors, telemetry streams, aggregated data, and image inputs from cameras, and in turn, autonomously provides analysis, solutions, and operational orders for specific circumstances, such as congested airport traffic. It works in cooperation with humans who can take control whenever a systematic solution provided by the system is not fit for occurrence. 

By displaying a bigger picture of the variables of a particular environment, this monitoring system provides an efficient solution to control and manage the use of natural resources such as energy or water. In the agriculture sector, it could offer open tools and protocols that assist farmers and researchers with collecting data and distributed experimental conditions that could help improve crop productivity and efficiency. When coupled with closed-loop pipetting technological solutions, connected with wireless sample temperature sensors, it could decrease the risk of errors and improve decision-making, while simultaneously allowing the users to keep track of costs and increase industrial and commercial efficiency.

# Future Perspectives

With the successful implementation of these remote monitoring systems, it will no longer be necessary to have as many people working on a daily basis on a farm, performing repetitive maintenance tasks. Despite the development of robotics and sensor technologies being applied in agriculture and other industries, the presence of human workers will likely be restricted to quality assurance, as they work fewer hours, while the machines take over hard tasks.

*Photo/Illustration: Framestock / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Fully automated border control and immigration departments with virtual agents, biometric identification, machine vision, truth assessments, and data analytics software to facilitate the movement and speed up the flow of people and goods within a country.
description.longText:
As globalization increases, huge volumes of travelers and immigrants, legitimate and illegitimate, make their way through border control every day. At the same time, customs need to handle the massive quantities of goods that enter countries.

In order to make this process safer, homeland security agencies collect data through traditional sources as well as social media and other open-sourced databases. In these cases, powerful machine learning techniques are employed in order to pinpoint risk. Authorities are then able to predict where to use their resources and where to target their interventions.

In addition, biometric identification and blockchain notaries destroy the industry of false documentation, creating new forms of securely verifying identification without relying on the human eye. Virtual agents equipped with machine vision can check if the visitor is telling the truth, while non-invasive systems (such as gamma rays or x-rays) inspect cargo and goods without the need for manual human assessment. All this data can be cross-checked in order to make customs nearly fool-proof while enforcing all laws approved by the respective ministries. 

# Future Perspectives

As different agencies upgrade their systems and integrate their processes, ports of entry could become immigration offices, allocating immigrants automatically after cross-checking information regarding territorial needs against the profile of the individual. The biggest challenge is to streamline systems to integrate all the information necessary to make a decision in a single click.

*Photo/illustration: ₢ Erik Odiin / unsplash.com*

description.shortText: A waste bin powered by machine vision, able to read in real-time the fill-level of the container. It automatically compacts waste, thus increasing storage capacity. It could help municipalities to increase recycling, as well as reduce their carbon footprint.
description.longText:
Automated bins powered by solar energy, able to compact waste autonomously as the container fills up. Scattered throughout the city, these bins decrease the pick-up frequency of regular bins required, as well as the volume of waste produced; an essential part of recycling.

Equipped with machine vision, the container can read the fill-level in real-time. As soon as the waste reaches capacity, it triggers a compaction mechanism that automatically compresses the trash, increasing the bin's capacity. The compaction system runs on solar-powered batteries, which enables the receptacles to work automatically. 

The smart waste containers are connected to a municipal network, providing information they collect through wireless transmission. Connection networks can combine cloud-based monitoring systems and data analytics platforms. 

# Future Perspectives

Municipalities aiming to increase recycling could place recycling collector units close to the compactor bins. It could enhance public awareness about recycling necessities while also reducing the carbon footprint.

*Photo/Illustration: Tupungato / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A short-range, low-latency data transfer network with decreased power consumption, which allows home appliances to interact by themselves. Integrated home appliances include security cameras, home cinema, lighting control, window treatments, cleaning robots, CO2 sensors, and swimming pools.
description.longText:
From personal assistants to thermostats, home appliances could sense the environment, learn from their owner's preferences and from live data from wearables, and change the home ambient, accordingly. By using a short-range, low-latency data transfer network and power consumption below that of conventional wi-fi technology, home appliances could improve the interaction among themselves. A whole range of systems, from security to home cinema, lighting control, window treatments, cleaning robots, CO2 sensors, and swimming pools, could exchange information and function autonomously.

Through the internet of things, appliances could become self-aware, by directly communicating to the cloud. Pill bottles could communicate with pharmacies to order refills, or smart fridges that sense and understand what items need to be replaced. Augmented toilets, for instance, would measure levels of hormones in urine or nutrients and microbiota levels in feces, and then inform the user about a possible pregnancy or any food deficiencies. Sensors in a garden might automatically activate security drones if any atypical activity is detected. In entertainment, the temperature and the lighting of the room might self-adjust according to the narrative to bring a more immersive experience.

According to the extended mind theory, people rely on their devices as an extension of their bodies, which creates a relationship of trust and dependence. A connected home-awareness system allows users to develop an in-depth knowledge of and deep connection with their homes, by taking control while obtaining a considerable amount of information. However, the fact that such devices are owned by private companies, who are entirely in charge of the software and operating systems, brings concerns regarding users' privacy or even body autonomy. In this sense, privacy regulations must be set both by governments and institutions to ensure that users' data is kept safe from the interest of companies.

# Future Perspectives

Home autonomy might get to the point where the house perfectly communicates with the outside world and begins working entirely autonomously. From grocery shopping to cleaning and maintenance, all home routines could be carried out without the necessity of humans, always according to homeowner preferences. New home appliances would then learn from the old ones, continuing to preserve the well-being and comfort of the homeowner.

Outside the house, other spaces might become interconnected. Appliances in public areas and shops could communicate with each other, sensing the current flow of people and reacting accordingly. One could argue that the private companies responsible for such algorithms would have control over parts of the users' intimate life, thus updating and changing the software at their will. Private companies could be able to take control over a portion of our minds and bodies, perhaps imperceptibly influencing personal decisions. In this scenario, the accuracy provided by these connections could simply display how vulnerable humans are in front of deeply aware devices.

*Photo / Illustration: © DaveFerencik / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A mobile app that provides citizens with legal support when they are pulled over by the police. When activated, the app displays information about legal rights, alerts the user's contact list about the situation, and records the audio field to audit the law enforcement later, if necessary.
description.longText:
A mobile application that provides citizens with the proper legal support whenever the police pull them over. The app provides legal rights education to users and law enforcement officers, making their encounters significantly more compliant. 

By merely clicking on the app icon when a police patrol approaches, the app instantly displays information about citizens' legal rights, thus orienting law enforcement limits and empowering the citizen. When activated, the app autonomously alerts the user's contact list about the situation through text message, while it records the audio field to audit the law enforcement later, if necessary. Finally, a “text-to-contact” feature can send the records along with text message alerts to emergency contacts previously determined by the user.

This mobile application could favor less unfair encounters with police officers and empower the citizenry to be informed about their rights. Besides invoking legal protection and empowering citizens, this tool could support a governmental response to alleged police misconduct, as the data generated can be admissible in court. 

# Future Perspectives

Real-time integrated report systems like the present mobile app can help with fair and more efficient policing, thus avoiding possible biases oriented towards race, social class, gender, etc. Also, this type of application could work directly with legal institutions, updating them with real-time information. The data collected could help raise a call for police education and society regarding biases and injustice.

*Photo/Illustration: Jacob Lund / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A water harvesting method that pulls moisture from the air and converts humidity into drinkable water. This framework promises to enable access to clean drinking water in low humidity areas or zones lacking access to water resources.
description.longText:
By pulling moisture from the air, this water harvesting framework can convert humidity into drinkable water. It functions either by extracting water droplets from coated filaments or by using water-attracting metal-organic devices to extract water from the atmosphere. 

Vapor can be harvested by sandwiching a layer of water-attracting metal-organic devices between a black painted surface. These devices are exceptionally efficient because they capture more water and require lower regeneration temperatures for their release compared to other sorbents. Generally, a device of this kind can produce three liters of water per day for every kilogram of metal-organic material. The other method occurs only in humidity affluent areas, where water droplets are formed on the coated filaments of a net, and then drop down into a collector. This collector has a design based on an alternative method using an underground air channel, which creates condensed water through a rapid cooling process.

This framework promises to enable access to clean drinking water in low humidity areas or zones lacking access to water resources. In agriculture, for instance, crops in arid regions would be irrigated with water coming for the atmosphere. The same logic could be applied to drip irrigation technologies, like the ones currently used in Israel in which a solid-state system is embedded into the pipes, thus saving billions of gallons of water per year.

# Future Perspectives

Water insecurity is a reality affecting thousands of people worldwide, and with climate change and an ever-growing population, this situation is expected to worsen accordingly. With water extracted from air moisture, used to irrigate plants and crops, and deliver drinkable water without harming natural resources, this technology not only offers a pathway to increase water availability but also to exploring extraterrestrial territories, in which the lack of access to drinkable water in spatial missions was always considered a burden.

description.shortText: AI software that supports legal prosecutions by automatically detecting and enforcing sentences. The Internet of Things would feed nearly unhackable data into the system to ensure informed decision-making while addressing law-breaking.
description.longText:
AI software that supports legal prosecution by automatically detecting and enforcing sentences, using historical data and harm assessment algorithms to analyze criminal databases. This software is fed with data derived from CCTV cameras and surveillance biometric recognition systems. The data is then turned into evidence, thus helping provide educational insights, enforce penalties for convicted criminals, or issue automatic fines and tickets. The algorithms could also be trained to give offenders a score to categorize the severity of their unlawful act. 

Different studies have proven that the information gathered by those devices could be used for criminal assessment, and function as a significant deterrent for bad behavior. The resulting predictions from these algorithms could help in pretrial, parole, and sentencing decisions. As automation takes over the judiciary and police systems, resources could be used more efficiently while saving capital. 

Private institutions could also use this technological solution by accessing and editing a cloud-based database. Establishments could share real-time CCTV camera content with the cloud for the system to analyze and send instant alerts whenever an intruder enters the establishment. The user can also alert the community at large when a crime occurs, adding images of the suspect(s) to watchlists and criminal databases.

However, this type of AI usage is subject to criticism because it could be used to reinforce societal biases. Solutions created to avoid algorithmic prejudices range from eliminating offensive and prejudicial content — usually designed under white-male perspectives — from algorithmic structures, to hiring a diverse team of developers consisting of minority groups. 


# Future Perspectives 

As judiciary systems around the world begin to see the potential of connected devices and artificial intelligence, surveillance and the usage of algorithms may become mandatory to keep the peace and keep criminals off the streets. Although the debate on issues of privacy, reinforcing bias and stereotypes continues, these subjects may be harder to justify, given the myriad of evidence and peace of mind that this technology could achieve. In the case of a private shared database, any user could be able to add a subject to the "criminal" list, thus creating a scenario of peer-based vigilance, in which every citizen is a node in a surveillance state.

*Photo/Illustration: Leszek / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A multi-level vertical center for crewless aerial vehicles shaped like giant towers to accommodate takeoff and landing of drones in dense urban settings. This solution would reduce the overall distance to customers and potentially reshape the way people receive packages.
description.longText:
A multi-level, vertically designed fulfillment center to make air logistics more fluid. It takes the shape of a giant beehive, and it is intended to accommodate the takeoff and landing of crewless aerial vehicles in dense urban settings. Also, uncrewed electric vehicles could visit the hub to charge their batteries.

Current studies for drone hubs were originally designed for delivery services. The drone hubs would work as a distribution center, enabling trucks to supply the hub through the ground entry, where workers or automated lifts would distribute the goods across the beehive for further drone delivery. 

As most of the current storage centers and warehouses are located on the outskirts of cities, the skyscraper beehive would solve this issue by scattering the drone hubs throughout the city. This solution would reduce the overall distance to customers and potentially reshape the way people receive packages, besides reducing the amount of carbon emissions emitted by fossil fuel vehicles. 

# Future perspectives

Besides being a drone port, these stations could potentially become a place of interaction between logistics and the city. By implementing cafes or building the drone hub close to a park, the mechanical and the human could meet, just like in train stations, for instance. 

Instead of building new structures to enable drone hubs, existing urban architecture could be adapted, thus reutilizing empty buildings in metropolises. As well as converting these structures, the surroundings would need to be adjusted, following the expected visual cues and parameters for the safe arrival and departure of drones. Therefore, architects, much like urban planners, would play an essential role in adapting cities in response to these unprecedented multidimensional spaces appropriately.

description.shortText: An economic framework that responds to individualized demands, acting upon actual individual intentions instead of vying for the attention of many. While altering the traditional supply-demand relationship, the intention economy can empower consumers to take a more proactive role in the market.
description.longText:
With the rise of analytics and big data, businesses could offer products and services targeted to more specific personal needs. Distinguishing from Attention Economy, this business model could bring individual sovereignty to customers over their data where they would, together with the sellers, decide the portion of their data they would like to disclose. 

Individualized demands could drive supply more directly, and vendors could respond to the actual intentions of customers instead of vying for the attention of many, thus possibly altering the traditional supply-demand relationship balance. The buyer notifies the market of the intent to buy, and sellers compete for the buyer’s purchase. Demand would drive supply far more directly and efficiently, while the need for and significance of advertising could diminish greatly.

On the other hand, entirely created personalized ads could become gold to advertisers, not to customers. In a fair case scenario of this economic model, clients would come to companies with their demands, proposals, ideas, and requirements, not the other way around. By transacting this way, clients could also increase the construction of their loyalty programs and rules, besides dictating their terms of service and payments.

In the shipping industry, the use of this sort of data could prevent unnecessary deliveries; only specific and regular orders would take place. In terms of welfare, healthcare systems could become more predictive than reactive; by enhancing government metrics, it may be possible to quantify citizens' desires and needs by location.

# Future Perspectives
In the long run, consumers may be able to improve the use of their data through increased collaboration between organizations, customers, and citizens. Although awareness of climate change has been growing, consumers often lack choices when purchasing sustainable products. In an economy where demand more directly drives supply, the voice of each consumer becomes stronger and has a more proactive role during negotiations.

description.shortText: A solar cell that combines two types of perovskite merged into a single photovoltaic cell. It is a low-cost alternative to conventional solar cell technologies, able to capture sunlight and efficiently convert it into electricity.
description.longText:
Composed of organic and inorganic elements, perovskite solar cells are a printable, low-cost alternative to conventional solar cell technology. It is able to capture sunlight and convert it into electricity efficiently. 

A perovskite structure is made of a mix of two layers that work as a sandwich, combining two types of perovskite merged into a single photovoltaic cell. When assembled, the top layer soaks up shorter wavelengths, while the bottom layer absorbs the remaining longer-wavelength light. One sheet contains metals like tin and iodine; the other contains lead and iodine laced with bromine. This combination of two solar cells can only be acquired when connected; as such, a single atom of hexagonal boron nitride separates the two layers. This single-atom-thick layer allows the top and bottom to work together in producing electricity.

The whole prospect of this technology is to make a more durable and easier to manufacture solar cells, simultaneously rapidly increasing the efficiency of energy conversion. Widely-used commercial solar cells made of polycrystalline silicon are costly to produce; albeit, popularly installed to power many devices and homes. Alternatively, the improved results produced by perovskite solar cells could mark a significant step towards the utilization of more affordable, renewable, and accessible forms of energy generation.

# Future Perspectives

Single-crystal perovskite films are low-cost and easy to process, with equal and possibly slightly greater efficiency rates compared to Si solar cell technology. Therefore, the production of a solar panel for grid-based electricity would be more attractive to markets, leading to increased adoption of solar cell technologies across the whole world. This technology creates novel perspectives regarding energy efficiency, including new application possibilities. Solar energy could be embedded in public transportation, substituting current carbon-based fuels, or alternatively, provide power for both domestic and industrial use.

Solar panel manufacturers could find themselves in an advantageous position if proper incentives and regulations fall into place. Adoption rates will skyrocket if governments are up to the challenge of adapting current urban infrastructure to embrace and integrate this technology into society. It would be costly to implement, but the outcomes are bright and favorable, especially regarding long-term durability.

description.shortText: Online and real-time monitoring of environmental parameters, like noise, light, and water, used as a solution for companies and municipal governments to control and manage city variables through a 3D visualization model.
description.longText:
Monitoring portals based on data measurements that provide direct insight into noise and vibration loads, water levels, energy use, lighting, air quality, safety, traffic flow, and so forth. After data crunching and collection, an urban web is modeled by converting all the data gathered into an online 3D model. This urban model contributes to the creation of more efficient, sustainable, and smarter surroundings.

This 3D model is part of the Building Information Modeling (BIM) concept, which is a digital representation of the physical and functional features of a place. By extending this concept to picture a possible BIM city, for instance, it could improve both knowledge and resource sharing, thus providing municipalities with a reliable basis for decision-making. It includes 3D maps of a city and real-time data, which could then be used in simulations and virtual tests of new solutions for urban planning issues. 

By defining classes and relations for geometric, topological, semantic, and visual properties, a city 3D digital platform would enable sophisticated tools and applications to simulate concepts, services, and planning. While taking advantage of a dynamic three-dimensional city model, this methodological approach for smarter cities could provide users with a collaborative data platform. Managers of this platform could take advantage of data collected from social media and apply the insights coming from popular opinion to design urban planning according to the public needs.

# Future Perspectives

As the 3D model of the entire urban area is updated continuously with real-time pictures and videos taken from CCTV cameras, this could raise privacy concerns over the lives of the citizens captured by these systems. In this sense, ethical and moral discussions would need to take place for this technology to be successfully deployed. Another solution for this issue is to employ real-time machine vision to automatically recognize and blur all human faces or even full bodies to help avoid possible voyeur-like tracking or spying on individuals.

description.shortText: A policy that applies environmental taxes for companies, industries, and countries depending on the amount of pollution they generate. It incentives sustainable practices by charging taxes when industries, companies, or countries do not comply with environmental regulatory standards.
description.longText:
A policy that incentives sustainable practices by charging taxes when industries, companies, or countries do not comply with environmental regulatory standards. If industries, for instance, have high carbon emission rates, the tax will automatically adjust the fee proportionally to the amount of CO2 produced. 

This policy model is instituted on a jurisdictional basis, which means administration representatives pay regular inspections to evaluate if companies and industries meet basic criteria. Internally, countries may also face examination from international boards to ensure environmental practices are being followed. The standards generally take into account the level of carbon emissions generated, as well as waste collection and recycling. If irregular procedures are detected, or if pollution rates exceed regulatory standards, taxation is applied according to the infraction committed. 

# Future Perspectives

This taxation model could speed up eco-friendly processes within companies, fostering innovation as the enterprise attempts to lower production-related environmental impacts. It could generate inter-company competition, leading to an arms race to be the quickest to lower tariffs based on the environment. On the other hand, vulnerable businesses may not be able to adapt to higher prices. As such, fiscal reforms could come with transitional solutions, enabling smallholders to adapt to change progressively. 

Blockchain technology could provide immutability regarding energy usage measurements, guaranteeing that companies and countries are making progress towards the agreed-upon goals.

*Photo/Illustration: Алексей Филатов / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: By bestowing trash with value, communities could build incentives to significantly reduce the quantity of waste carted away to landfills. Collectors could convert plastic waste into cash or other assets, such as food, fuel, schooling, public transportation, or mobile phone charging vouchers.
description.longText:
Plastic waste is now so ubiquitous in our environment that it has even been suggested it could serve as a geological indicator of the Anthropocene era. Rather than viewing it as garbage, organizations are starting to empower local communities by paying them to collect waste and bring it to collection centers, a business model commonly known as 'waste as a currency.' In this model, plastic waste is processed into pellets and sold to companies above market value as a recycled raw material.

Collectors could convert plastic waste into cash or other goods, such as food, fuel, or vouchers for schooling, public transportation, or mobile phone charging. Some initiatives use a blockchain-based banking system to convert the weight of plastic into an online token accepted in several local businesses and services. Also, urban recycling platforms are starting to use digital currencies to reward good behavior, paying users for properly separating recyclables. Rewards can include discounts and other bonuses at local businesses in the neighborhood.

This system stimulates growth by encouraging collectors and citizens to become small-scale entrepreneurs and is highly desirable in sustainability terms. It acts as a closed-loop system that directly recycles the waste it creates. Further, by offering unskilled workers the chance to improve their household incomes, inequalities may decrease while reducing the demand for the production of new plastic.

# Future Perspectives
Consumers are becoming increasingly aware of how their habits impact the environment, to the point some brands started to accept waste as a form of payment. By taking waste as a currency for goods to enhance positive perceptions, it allows previously wasteful brands to align themselves with eco-conscious customers. Additionally, by bestowing trash with value, companies are building incentives that should significantly reduce the quantity of waste sent to landfills.

Geopolitical problems could emerge from this type of currency if it becomes too widespread and accepted as a commodity. Corrupt governments, for example, could start to produce waste as a means of accumulating the reward that comes from it or incentivizing entire communities to make as much trash as possible. Although, with the constant evolution of remanufacturing techniques, the overproduction of waste could become a means to support these initiatives and further counteract the possible threats coming from corruption.

description.shortText: A virtual, customized, and idealized version of oneself employed to serve as an interface in digital interpersonal communications. It allows representation in digital environments and improved interaction between peers online.
description.longText:
A virtual representation of an entity, generally a person. Avatars could be single images, two-dimensional characters, nonhuman beings, tridimensional embodiment, or a mix of digital elements and an edited physical image. This digital embodiment mostly serves as interface for communication between people, and occurs as a representation of one's social presence online and chosen identity form.

Unlike the human physical form, which relies on biological limitations and genetic factors, an avatar could be created and easily altered by its creator. Such digital choices and alterations range from natural adjustments, such as gender flexibility, hair color, different body proportions to nonhuman features like an unusual number of limbs or mouths, none of which has to match a person's physical embodiment. As avatars could be shape-shifted across media types, an individual could decide to have multiple representations, depending on mood or platform. In this way, a person’s identity would become something dynamic and malleable. 

Augmented reality platforms could help enhance specific features and add digital elements to physical faces and bodies with the help of face recognition and tracking. With the popularization of face filters, there is an increasing trend of remaining forever younger, fitter, and more attractive online. On one hand, it appears that body homogenization is inevitable; on the other, this new freedom of identity could represent a diversity of self and artistic representations like never seen before. The ability to curate one's identity could be a freeing experience, especially for people suffering from mental-health disorders such as body dysmorphia. 

# Future Perspectives

As the time spent online and the interaction in digital spheres increases, it is expected that people will likely start to rely on avatars as their true self-representations. Once simulations look and feel more real than the physical realm, avatars are counted upon to become the closest embodiment of an individual's character, thus surpassing the limitations of a person's physical traits.

With the help of mind upload, a person could then live permanently in a virtual world, or metaverse, forever inhabiting their avatar. Purely digital beings or uploaded minds could choose to come back to the physical realm, occupying robotic bodies or humanoid physical avatars. In this scenario, avatars cease to be purely digital proxies to become the user’s primary body.

description.shortText: Sterilization robots that draw ozone gas from the atmosphere to eliminate pathogenic microorganisms from surfaces.
description.longText:
A disinfection robot, designed to draw ozone gas from the atmosphere to sterilize frequently touched surfaces against bacteria, viruses, and microorganisms. The robot generates ozone gas from the surrounding environment and converts it back to oxygen, requiring only water and electricity to perform sterilization. 

The place to be disinfected is sealed and evacuated, and then the robot increases the room's humidity and releases the ozone gas. The released gas can disinfect surfaces on the hospital's bed rails and tables, pumps, light switches, and doorknobs. The machine updates itself at regular intervals and ensures that the disinfection cycle is progressing efficiently. 

The robot includes the help of machine vision to avoid collisions with other objects or detect the presence of humans in the room, stopping the disinfection process immediately as ozone is highly harmful to human health. Connected to a network of IoT devices, such as tablets, computers, or an operational command center, the functions of the robot are monitored by trained staff and can be remotely controlled at any time. 

# Future perspectives

Ozone-decontamination robots could also exist outside hospital facilities, helping clean other kinds of surfaces. High-traffic places such as metro stations, crowded workplaces, and other public spaces could be cleaned by those robots, reducing potential contagious diseases.

*Photo/Illustration: jiravut / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: An interactive, personalized assistant powered by AI software, integrated with a variety of data sources. It can make purchases, find the best deals, suggest alternatives that better fit specific user needs, or even create complete retirement plans for the elderly autonomously.
description.longText:
By tracking user habits, interests, and activities, financial advisors can provide a tailor-made service that meets and anticipates the unique, changing needs of each user. By comparing offers from multiple merchants, looking for the option to pay in alternative currencies, and managing user investment accounts around the clock, this technology also improves financial transparency, helping customers make more informed decisions. Fraudulent transactions can be reduced by monitoring user behavioral patterns, identifying anomalies, and when necessary, immediately creating an alert.

The financial assistant uses a variety of systems and methods that could help make a purchase following user-determined steps, such as suggesting alternative products, determining availability in stores, searching for the absolute lowest prices, selecting the payment method to then execute the purchase, etc. Deep Learning could help the assistant make sense of immense amounts of data, automatically tracking, pulling, and crossing-checking information from different sources to create user-tailored conclusions. Additionally, through the use of Predictive Analytics Trading, money can be automatically invested depending on market conditions, the user’s available funds, and personal risk profile.

Using Voice Identification, the user could be automatically authenticated, eliminating the need to remember a password or answer repetitive security questions. Natural language processing would allow users to conversationally interact with their assistant as if they were talking to a human financial advisor available 24/7, entirely dedicated to each customer's individual needs.

The financial advisor will be able to calculate mortgages, create a college financial plan, send and request payments to/from any authorized contact, get the latest updates on commercial markets, pull up foreign exchange rates, and even create a retirement plan. For the elderly, who often have difficulties in operating modern banking applications, tailored conversational finance assistance, with unlimited patience, could be especially useful. Measures regarding data protection are especially necessary, as the assistant would be cloud-based, and a significant amount of sensitive data would be stored. It could theoretically be hacked, thus exposing all the user's financial choices and even allowing the attacker to freely move around assets without the user's consent. It is especially important to take privacy protocols seriously and ensure that those managing the backends of these intelligent systems undergo proper training.

# Future Perspectives

The more data sources made available to a financial advisor, the better it will be at giving advice and performing useful actions beyond simple exchanges. By integrating with public data sources and taking millions of data points from the user’s history into account, the assistant could calculate how moving to a new state would affect retirement planning, for example.

A layer of abstraction would connect different information platforms to maximize the potential of future personal assistants. Although the personal assistants of today excel at resolving simple requests, these systems still perform poorly at following up on longer-term plans and analyzing new information based on experience. Deep reinforcement learning algorithms, together with memory attention models, could allow the agents to plan for longer-term goals with specific dependencies.

For finance, emotionless decision-making, another advantage of virtual assistants, provides level-headed thinking in moments of crisis in order to develop recommended solutions or advise against impulse purchases – replacing emotion-based decisions with data-driven ones. Furthermore, those who cannot afford a human financial advisor will have access to a tailored one at an even cheaper rate, increasing the reach of professional financial advice, regardless of income class.

Although every financial assistant could be trained using specific data from each user, the overall capabilities of the algorithm would remain the same. Handing important life choices over to automated decision-makers requires immense trust that the system will make your personal priorities, theirs. Accordingly, a scenario in which the same financial assistant becomes popular among many people will end up causing an inevitable paradox: whose interests will the algorithm really serve? Is it possible to maintain the rules of the free market in a world in which every decision-maker has access to all known data at any given moment? Or even, in a world in which the main decisions are made by extremely complex algorithms that can make sense of immense amounts of data in a fraction of a second, what power is really left for humans?

*Photo: © Adeolu Eletu / unsplash.com*
description.longTextHtml:
By tracking user habits, interests, and activities, financial advisors can provide a tailor-made service that meets and anticipates the unique, changing needs of each user. By comparing offers from multiple merchants, looking for the option to pay in alternative currencies, and managing user investment accounts around the clock, this technology also improves financial transparency, helping customers make more informed decisions. Fraudulent transactions can be reduced by monitoring user behavioral patterns, identifying anomalies, and when necessary, immediately creating an alert.

The financial assistant uses a variety of systems and methods that could help make a purchase following user-determined steps, such as suggesting alternative products, determining availability in stores, searching for the absolute lowest prices, selecting the payment method to then execute the purchase, etc. Deep Learning could help the assistant make sense of immense amounts of data, automatically tracking, pulling, and crossing-checking information from different sources to create user-tailored conclusions. Additionally, through the use of Predictive Analytics Trading, money can be automatically invested depending on market conditions, the user’s available funds, and personal risk profile.

Using Voice Identification, the user could be automatically authenticated, eliminating the need to remember a password or answer repetitive security questions. Natural language processing would allow users to conversationally interact with their assistant as if they were talking to a human financial advisor available 24/7, entirely dedicated to each customer's individual needs.

The financial advisor will be able to calculate mortgages, create a college financial plan, send and request payments to/from any authorized contact, get the latest updates on commercial markets, pull up foreign exchange rates, and even create a retirement plan. For the elderly, who often have difficulties in operating modern banking applications, tailored conversational finance assistance, with unlimited patience, could be especially useful. Measures regarding data protection are especially necessary, as the assistant would be cloud-based, and a significant amount of sensitive data would be stored. It could theoretically be hacked, thus exposing all the user's financial choices and even allowing the attacker to freely move around assets without the user's consent. It is especially important to take privacy protocols seriously and ensure that those managing the backends of these intelligent systems undergo proper training.

Future Perspectives

The more data sources made available to a financial advisor, the better it will be at giving advice and performing useful actions beyond simple exchanges. By integrating with public data sources and taking millions of data points from the user’s history into account, the assistant could calculate how moving to a new state would affect retirement planning, for example.

A layer of abstraction would connect different information platforms to maximize the potential of future personal assistants. Although the personal assistants of today excel at resolving simple requests, these systems still perform poorly at following up on longer-term plans and analyzing new information based on experience. Deep reinforcement learning algorithms, together with memory attention models, could allow the agents to plan for longer-term goals with specific dependencies.

For finance, emotionless decision-making, another advantage of virtual assistants, provides level-headed thinking in moments of crisis in order to develop recommended solutions or advise against impulse purchases – replacing emotion-based decisions with data-driven ones. Furthermore, those who cannot afford a human financial advisor will have access to a tailored one at an even cheaper rate, increasing the reach of professional financial advice, regardless of income class.

Although every financial assistant could be trained using specific data from each user, the overall capabilities of the algorithm would remain the same. Handing important life choices over to automated decision-makers requires immense trust that the system will make your personal priorities, theirs. Accordingly, a scenario in which the same financial assistant becomes popular among many people will end up causing an inevitable paradox: whose interests will the algorithm really serve? Is it possible to maintain the rules of the free market in a world in which every decision-maker has access to all known data at any given moment? Or even, in a world in which the main decisions are made by extremely complex algorithms that can make sense of immense amounts of data in a fraction of a second, what power is really left for humans?

description.shortText: An offshore wind turbine mounted on a floating structure that generates electricity in water depths where fixed-foundation turbines are not feasible. Floating wind turbines, when stabilized by anchors and a buoyant substructure, can generate more electricity than current wind propellers.
description.longText:
One of wind power's most known hurdles is intermittency. Yet, the offshore wind of water deeper than 60 meters blows uninterruptedly, thus offering a constant and more stable source to harvest the energy coming from wind power. To take advantage of offshore wind, turbines mounted on floating structures present a promising solution to generate electricity.

Floating wind turbines, made of floating windmills stabilized by anchors and a buoyant substructure, can generate more electricity than current ground wind propellers. The worlds' first floating wind farm, for instance, which took 15 years to build, consists of five floating windmills, 154 meters in diameter, each standing on top of a 3,800-ton buoyant substructure, held down by three anchors, can generate enough electricity to power 4,000 homes.

However, while these structures are technically feasible, they are not yet economically viable, as doing anything offshore is highly expensive. The cost of constructing, installing, operating, monitoring, maintaining, and decommissioning infrastructure of this scale, in the ocean, is costly, and dealing with such a large and complex structure is no trivial task.

# Future Perspectives

With the help of autonomous robots used to control offshore engineering activities, from investigating the seabed to operating, inspecting, and maintaining floating wind turbines, this solution could one day reach wide-range adoption. Besides, machine learning models could assist operations by spotting continuous errors and building patterns to avoid further abnormal issues, sparing workers the risks imposed in offshore inspections.

*Photo/illustration: ₢  Shaun Dakin / unsplash.com*

description.shortText: A visual token for achievements, affiliations, authorizations, and other trust relationships used as a means to certify such procedures across the web, representing a specific asset that is covered and thus certified by associated verification organizations, such as universities and schools.
description.longText:
A visual token for achievements, affiliations, authorizations, and other trust relationships that could be used as a means to certify such procedures across the web, would represent a specific asset that is covered and thus certified by associated verification organizations. This certification system is designed to verify and support individuals by empowering them for the online or physical/in-person skills they have achieved, with no need for validation from a standard or traditional educational institute.

In addition, while placing the responsibility for their behavior back on the student, encouragement and other forms of social approval should go in line with the tokens. Consequently, it would increase student engagement in the classroom and students would be motivated to attend classes regularly. 

# Future Perspectives

By introducing extrinsic rewards such as points and badges, healthy competitions would be promoted among students because they would only earn points and badges when taking part in classroom activities. However, the demand could be variable as the targeted problems may vary according to student levels. In that case, a fixed system wouldn't make sense to implement as different, more dynamic rules would need to be developed in line with the individuality and diversity of each classroom.

*Photo/illustration: ₢ Emile Perron / unsplash.com*

description.shortText: A device embedded with sensors designed to physically interact with virtual objects and environments. Overall, it allows users to tactilely explore virtual data, enabling them to manage and change the properties of the virtual object with the movement of their fingers and hands.
description.longText:
As virtual, computer-generated environments become more prevalent through video games, virtual-reality environments, or even installations using sensors, users could go beyond visual stimulation with the help of simulated touch, pressure, force, and other sensations. Kinaesthetic communication devices are most commonly worn on the fingers, allowing someone to use their hands as if they were in a typical environment.

These interactive systems collect information and data regarding dexterity, the senses, or eye movement, and help users handle real and virtual objects. Some simulations may let the user tactilely explore virtual data, enabling them to manage and change the properties of the virtual object with the movement of their fingers and hands. While current systems are operated using joysticks or handheld devices, these could be a hindrance when trying to recreate more natural interactions. 

Applications in education could make it possible for students to understand concepts such as force or resistance, or even model geometric figures and virtual sculptures. People could also simulate and improve learning through this type of technology, enabling them to understand the consequences of their actions in a safe and controlled virtual environment. Similar to the way virtual reality controllers enable painting in an immersive environment, this technology adds touch response, creating another layer for users to interact with virtual reality. 

# Future Perspectives 

In the future, these devices could help doctors remotely perform surgeries with better feedback responses than those currently available. By using telerobots instead of attempting to identify partially or wholly obscured organs visually, virtual surgery simulators could support surgeons to complete their procedures with more precision and simplicity. It could also assist with maintenance or repairs, thus enabling employees from anywhere in the world to guide on-site users with precision, decreasing the number of trips necessary for specialists to take. For emergencies, these devices could be readily available.

As VR environments grow in popularity, the importance of translating body movements and body language into those worlds becomes essential. The internet is dominated by written and verbal communication, letting other forms of communication fall short. But, gestures and body language are essential, especially for the complex communication of emotions and mental states.

description.shortText: Through a smartphone or an AR device, a digital interactive layer is added to the customer shopping journey. Online and physical shoppers are provided with a more informed, frictionless, immersive, and hyper-personalized experience.
description.longText:
Through a smartphone or an AR device, Augmented Reality brings a more immersive experience for shopping from home. Brands could create digital stores that enable instant purchases in an ultra-personalized tool that works in an interactive 3D visualization. 

A user could, for instance, access the AR shopping platform, choose the store that fits their preferences better, and test a furniture in their living room. Users could select the color of the product and even design modular pieces. Consumers could also blend their make-up or try different clothes with simple gestures. This platform is expected to become a robust virtual branding tool as stores are expected to become virtual meeting points, where brands become social platforms for customers. 

# Future Perspectives

In a brick-and-mortar building, this technological solution could gather a series of in-store interfaces and data analytics that provide dynamic shopping suggestions and assistance. People would be able to speak or type in natural language and ask where specific products are located or what services are available in a particular store. In return, they receive relevant, customized responses. It would include product reviews, examples of similar products, location of products in-store, instructions, or an option to buy online. As consumers grow more thoughtful about their consumption habits, information such as carbon print, local producers, and fair-trade could also come into play.

Since the Covid-19 pandemic, AR solutions might gain popularity, especially in the personal care industry. With the advancement of this technology, brands may start to leverage the use of augmented reality as try-on platforms. However, as the purchase process is exceptionally frictionless, it may result in overspending. This technology could offer ways to avoid that by creating wealth management visualizations, as well as the individual’s financial behavior through interactive infographics on how money is being spent, translating visually crucial information. 

Privacy is also a growing concern among consumers. As AR payment options emerge, both companies and consumers should place privacy matters at the forefront. Hacking of AR apps is a concern, mainly because these experiences are more intimate than traditional shopping methods and could track biometric data and potential conversations. Also, this could lead to another matter, such as misinformation and deep fakes.

description.shortText: A wastewater treatment method that benefits from the rapid growth rate, lipid accumulation richness, and carbon neutrality of algae to remove pollutants from wastewater treatment facilities in factories or municipal level plants.
description.longText:
As algae can be incredibly resilient to the effect of toxic contaminant concentration — a common scenario found in organic wastewater — they can help remediate the contamination in water bodies due to the unprecedented amount of waste discharged in the ecosystem worldwide. Wastewater algae treatments can be independently applied or even associated with conventional wastewater treatment facilities in factories or municipal level plants, where they help decrease the overall costs of aeration.

Scientific and empirical studies have demonstrated noteworthy results with many algae species such as Euglenia, Scenedesmus, Selenastrum, Chlorella, and Actinastrum. These algae naturally process some pollutants and nutrients commonly found in wastewater. They break inorganic nutrients down into organic matter, remove phosphorus, phosphate, and other hazardous contaminants and pathogens such as E. coli and fecal coliform from wastewater. 

Algae also don't require clean water or extensive land to grow. Closed-loop photobioreactors with glass piping and controlled lighting are the favorite format for recent mass application at the municipal level since algal and nutrient ratio can be measured, sustaining optimal conditions for algae growth 24/7. To improve the quality of the treated water in a biological process, this kind of treatment can be paired with other microorganisms such as heterotrophic bacteria that also use pollutants as a food source.

Algae are shown to be effective in cleaning and recovering nutrients, but also in the production of decentralized and affordable food, large-scale protein substitutions, biofuel production, cosmetics, and drugs. However, the separation of biomass from water, process efficiency in cold climates, and optimal species association still represent technical setbacks.

# Future perspectives

The rapid worldwide population growth observed in recent times, associated with intense urbanization and agricultural production, has generated an unprecedented irregular discharge of wastewater into rivers, lakes, and oceans. This situation exacerbates many biological hazards by introducing excess pollutants and nutrients into the environment, affecting the delicate stability of worldwide aquatic resources. Nutrients widely found in wastewater, such as phosphorus and nitrogen, decrease water oxygen levels, thus causing overfertilization, which leads to the decline of biodiversity in these environments.

Developing countries have significant responsibility for wastewater mismanagement, and it is precisely in natural landscapes in those regions, with humid, sun-exposed environment, which algae thrive best. Their characteristics make them an asset to be associated with the solutions to many established problems, especially with the excellent ratio between their costs and benefits. As microalgae cultures offer a clean solution to treat inorganic nitrogen and phosphorus in tertiary and quandary treatments, it makes it feasible in the future to remove heavy metals as well as inorganic compounds from water bodies and prevent secondary pollution.

description.shortText: An energy transfer system that charges batteries of onboard vehicles by creating an alternating electromagnetic field with an in-vehicle induction coil. It could allow electric vehicles to forgo heavy batteries, decrease their weight, increase their effectiveness, and reduce manufacturing costs.
description.longText:
An energy transfer system applied to roads and highways, able to charge batteries of onboard vehicles by creating an alternating electromagnetic field with an in-vehicle induction coil. The system can be used to charge parked vehicles using fixed pods or moving vehicles in a ‘dynamic charging’ method through electrified roads. Thanks to its convenience and reliability, it could completely disrupt vehicle-oriented power infrastructures and has the potential to make the range for cars and drones limitless. It would allow electric vehicles to forgo heavy batteries, decreasing their weight, increasing their effectiveness, and reducing manufacturing costs. 

This solution is attracting attention, mainly because it can be applied to existing road structures. Once a roadway is outfitted with this solution, it can continuously power adequately equipped vehicles. The system could accurately calculate the vehicle’s energy consumption, enabling the electricity costs per vehicle to be passed onto the owner or user. Additionally, wireless charging could become bidirectional: not only from the road to the vehicle but vice versa by harnessing the energy generated from braking.

One of the main drawbacks includes the slow inductive electric charging compared to its plug-based counterpart. Also, this technological solution is more expensive to produce and demands inductive compatibility to function. Ideally, the city and manufacturers would work together, providing a one-size-fits-all compatible charger. Yet, in a globalized world, drivers that cross borders between countries repeatedly may face essential challenges regarding compatibility. 

# Future Perspectives
Since battery storage plays a crucial role in enabling the broad adoption of electric vehicles, this technology could have disruptive effects over transportation infrastructure — already increasingly migrating towards electric-powered vehicles. Besides, it could infinitely extend the operational range of cars and drones while simultaneously altering urban power distribution infrastructure. While national grids are increasingly moving away from coal and oil, this technology is a natural and logical choice to be integrated with renewable sources of energy, such as solar and kinetic power.

description.shortText: With the help of blockchain, schools could have access to students' school records from institutions they have studied previously. This protocol would help the educational sector to keep track of students' development more closely and precisely.
description.longText:
By precisely knowing where students come from, including their educational backgrounds, classes could be adapted to suit their needs better. Through a decentralized platform in the blockchain ledger, education tracking could make verification and recording transitions free of fraud. 

This technological solution could potentially reduce false claims of unearned educational credits by issuing blockchain-based certificates unable to be falsified. Students' e-portfolios could be verified, while the distributed ledger checks, secure, and shares educational records. Institutions would have access to a student's curriculum, and digital academic transcripts would be managed with more accuracy. This protocol would establish more transparent systems and create more accountability of academic achievements between students and schools as blockchain would allow both professors and students to track the entire learning process. 

Another exciting aspect is the use of  “smart contracts” while issuing and validating certificates in the blockchain. They would have the potential to reduce paperwork significantly, and they could be applied to verify students' attendance or assignment completion. School or university libraries might as well use this protocol to expand their services by creating an enhanced metadata archive of their collections.

# Future Perspectives

In the face of the refugee crisis, education is a critical aspect of the international refugee response. Simple actions such as enrollment become difficult as host institutions cannot have access to people's educational records. In order to deliver a more inclusive and quality education for all, private and governmental institutions could have some of this process made more manageable, as they use a blockchain educational tracking system in the admission processes.

description.shortText: The combination of the Internet of things, sensors, the blockchain, and real-time monitoring could help track products, and provide a full-service solution for farmers as well as consumers to help avoid waste and food loss throughout the supply chain.
description.longText:
Pinpointing the primary sources of food waste at restaurants, hospitals, schools, houses, and other buildings may be the first step to recapturing or saving millions of uneaten and wasted food products around the world. Implementing a software platform that tracks food inventory, records purchasing and expiration dates as well as the reason for discarding food could help detect weak points in the established product journeys. Touchscreens and other easy-to-use interfaces could further facilitate the adoption of this type of technology by allowing employees, cooks, and other personnel to make instant notes about food being discarded.

Besides the intentional discarding of leftovers, there is also spoilage and loss of food during transportation from the farm to the processing factory; additionally, vegetables and fruits are typically selected (or not) solely based on visual qualities. This technology could also help avoid cases where producers have a larger supply than demand, and food ends up rotting somewhere along the supply chain. It is estimated that post-harvest waste happens partly when temperature-sensitive products are not managed correctly. To prevent this, sensors and the Internet of things could help track produce and precisely map where precisely along the chain losses take place. Additionally, they could provide information about food quality and whether discarding products, at any given stage, is essential or not.

# Future Perspectives
Together with other tools such as blockchain, it would be possible to track the origin of the food by monitoring and registering all the information that could help avoid losses along the entirety of the supply chain. Besides, software on mobile phones and smart household appliances could provide real-time information about quality, ripening stage, etc. for end consumers in their own houses or in stores.

The quantity of food wasted by citizens in both developed and developing countries is alarming, especially considering how, after a somewhat stable decline, hunger has increased again in the last decade. The recovery of food surpluses, therefore, is gaining much-needed attention, creating a market for innovative solutions based on information and communication technologies. Several mobile applications attempt to reduce domestic food waste by introducing a “food sharing” model. Current practices to recover surplus foodstuffs in consumable conditions are still unable to reach the vast majority of food waste. Effective solutions will need to integrate at different stages of the supply chain, and take into account uses besides exclusively human consumption.

This technology could also help avoid cases where producers have a larger supply than demand, and food ends up rotting somewhere along the supply chain. It is estimated that post-harvest waste happens partly when temperature-sensitive products are not managed correctly. To prevent this, sensors and the Internet of things could help track produce and precisely map where precisely along the chain losses take place. Additionally, they could provide information about food quality and whether discarding products, at any given stage, is essential or not.

Future Perspectives

Together with other tools such as blockchain, it would be possible to track the origin of the food by monitoring and registering all the information that could help avoid losses along the entirety of the supply chain. Besides, software on mobile phones and smart household appliances could provide real-time information about quality, ripening stage, etc. for end consumers in their own houses or in stores.

The quantity of food wasted by citizens in both developed and developing countries is alarming, especially considering how, after a somewhat stable decline, hunger has increased again in the last decade. The recovery of food surpluses, therefore, is gaining much-needed attention, creating a market for innovative solutions based on information and communication technologies. Several mobile applications attempt to reduce domestic food waste by introducing a “food sharing” model. Current practices to recover surplus foodstuffs in consumable conditions are still unable to reach the vast majority of food waste. Effective solutions will need to integrate at different stages of the supply chain, and take into account uses besides exclusively human consumption.

description.shortText: A robust encrypted database that safely stores e-citizen data and withstands any cyberattack with the ability to reboot an entire country in an instant. Like a traditional embassy, it has sovereign rights and is located outside the state of ownership.
description.longText:
A data backup embassy is a robust encrypted database that withstands any cyberattack. It works as a storage facility that guarantees digital continuity to vast amounts of sensitive data such as medical history, social security, and corporate information. Similarly to a typical embassy that functions based on sovereign rights, it would be located outside the physical borders of the country.

In emergency cases, it could reboot an entire country in an instant, thus helping a country to overcome botnet attacks quickly with denial-of-service programming, an algorithm that prevents digital services from running. By working as a cloud-based extension of public digital services, only the physical hardware storing the database would be transnational. However, the government would continue to have complete sovereignty over the information stored inside.

Though it helps protect data against cyberattacks, the creation of a transnational database would also keep citizen data safe and accessible even in the event of an attack by a foreign military. The same protection applies to power outages, natural disasters, or any other type of calamity. With this strategy, a country could have its public services up and running again in no time. 

Currently, there are many challenges regarding how international laws could adhere to this technology. An international agreement concerning modern storage methods of government data should establish a global methodology for this technology to be deployed. It should include, especially regarding the principles of protecting public safety, individual privacy and transparency frameworks to deal with, and store sensitive data.

# Future Perspectives

To keep such an immense amount of information physically stored in the same place undoubtedly increases both the focus and intensity of cyber-attacks and data theft. The storage system could use a virtual model for data in a privately owned public cloud that could provide different functionalities, such as auto-scaling and geographically spread application instances, which could help mitigate attacks. 

If coupled with the blockchain technology, instead of securing system vulnerabilities with one or a few transnational data embassies, thousands of computers could serve together as one extensive backup database. By doing this, it would ensure the safety of not only e-citizenship data but also public services and individual user data as well.

An effective way to store such information would be through DNA-based storage systems with the capability of storing an incredible amount of data while occupying very little physical space. Although this method of storage could still be physically stolen, it would eliminate the chances of cyber-attacks; for the time being, system hacking is non-existent against DNA-storage media.

description.shortText: An energy storage solution that harvests, stores, and converts atmospheric air into potential energy. As it does not rely on natural resources besides atmospheric air to work, this solution promises both applicability and scalability. The energy container is easy to transport and cheap to replicate.
description.longText:
An energy harvester container, designed to extract, store, and convert atmospheric air into potential energy. By exposing the air to extremely low temperatures, liquid air energy storage (LAES) can transform and conserve the air in a liquified state. 

First, the air is cooled inside the equivalent of giant thermos flasks at low temperatures of around -195 degrees C. As the liquid air is stored at almost ambient pressure, the energy density becomes very high, only requiring small storage space. In order to extract energy from the storage compartments, the liquid air is exposed to the environment temperature that heats it up, returning it to a gaseous state. As liquid air is released back into a gaseous form, its expansion can power the turbines that put the energy back into the grid. 

# Future Perspectives

Long-duration energy storage solutions today usually face geographical restrictions on the amount of sunlight or wind flows that enable solar and wind power plants to function. As LAES does not rely on natural resources besides atmospheric air to work, this solution is promising both in applicability and scalability. The energy container is easy to transport and cheap to replicate. 

Current prototypes work on differing air conditions, even in more polluted or industrial areas. Accordingly, this solution shows excellent potential in generating clean energy in a reasonably effortless process and can help mitigate the effects produced by gas emissions on the atmosphere.

*Photo/Illustration: Franco Nadalin / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A means of using the infrastructure of the blockchain to certify and authenticate procedures, courses, identification, and educational validations.
description.longText:
A means of using the infrastructure of blockchain technology to certify and authenticate procedures, courses, identification, and educational validations. The process begins with the recipient's request for a certificate from the institution (i.e., school) with the support of a digital certificate wallet. The institution issues a certificate to the requesting user, who will be able to share this document with their employer or any other institutions requiring this type of confirmation.

By using blockchain and cryptography at schools and educational institutions, it creates a certification infrastructure that puts both the student and the institution itself in control of full individual records of achievements and accomplishments, from independent courses to a particular subject at school. This hands-on token for accomplishments, affiliations, authorizations and other trust relationships could be used as a means to certify such procedures across the web. 

These certificates also represent a specific asset that is covered and thus certified by associated verification organizations without the need to pass through bureaucratic hoops. Besides, it guarantees universities and educational establishments can safely publicly issue diplomas in an encrypted format, protecting individual privacy. The diploma user-owner would receive a URL link requesting access, and following a simple procedure (granting permission from a quick confirmatory click or even allowing access through the Ethereum), the data is decrypted. No login or password is required: only the holder can decide whether to communicate the link on platforms and/or with possible recruiters.

# Future Perspectives
In order to make these certifications significant according to their competencies, widespread and clear recognition of the value of different products is going to be a key factor. While some platforms rely on prestigious colleges and the extensive quality assessment processes that already exist to connect both parties, other solutions include digital badges and tokens that could include blockchain as a means to validate such courses.

These certifications could ensure that countries and institutions which deal with problems such as money laundering and corruption could have a reliable and unhackable way of understanding the origin and the usages of their cryptocurrencies. For example, governments could make this technology mandatory when using public funding, in order to ensure that it was spent as initially intended.

description.shortText: By combining computational fluid dynamics with machine learning and meteorological data-sources, this system steadily improves the ability and accuracy to forecast both weather and natural incidents with far-reaching results for individuals and businesses.
description.longText:
By combining computational fluid dynamics with machine learning and meteorological data-sources, a predictive weather system provides a more accurate alternative to current weather prediction models. This dynamic and fluid forecast software aggregates a multitude of climate and weather-related data. This data is later rated, ranked, and weighted by machine learning to process immediate comparisons between historical data and weather forecasts. Used in this way, weather models could more efficiently take into account inaccuracies, such as overestimated rain predictions or even to perform more accurate predictions.

Apart from developing rankings, machine-learning models that use deep learning show promising results in predicting cyclones, atmospheric rivers, weather fronts, and forest fires, and can even assess deforestation. With better predictions of climate, it may be possible to modify decisions to decrease undesirable impacts and take better advantage of expected favorable conditions. 

Farmers, for instance, could be better prepared to make decisions regarding crop management with the inclusion of the ideal window for sowing, fertilizing, weeding, and harvesting. In the case of urban planners, simulation models can be useful to adapt both existing projects and upcoming developments in order to make them more responsive to the consequences of climate change (for instance, reducing heat islands and adaptation of areas prone to flood), as well as more accountable to the measurements and policies that regulate emissions.

# Future Perspectives

Gathering and processing high-quality data of potential environmental risks will continuously be a need for both future and present-day society. Improving accuracy in weather prediction can have far-reaching implications, not just for disaster mitigation, but also for businesses that rely on commodity futures trading or other weather-based factors. Due to the amount of data that needs to be analyzed, advancements in the quantum computing area should directly impact the accuracy of these forecasting systems.

Also, by combining this software with new infrared remote atmospheric sounding systems with cloud-penetrating microwave radiometers, space-borne radar, light detection and ranging (LiDAR), as well as remote sensing observations from the ground, it could create a sensor web around the globe for future views of the Earth. These new and improved weather and climate products are also leading to new industries, like “weather derivatives.” Weather derivatives are financial solutions that help weather-sensitive companies spread out and insure themselves against their inherent risks.
