description.shortText: An international identity document that is not attached to any nation-state. It could allow stateless people to change their legal status, but also redefine equality by positioning it as a relationship among co-members of a global society and not one among national citizens.
description.longText:
The World Passport consists of a document provided by nonprofit organizations that rely on the human right to travel to give undocumented people actual papers. In a globalized world like ours, we face an increasing degree of convergence between nations in terms of economic thinking and technique. However, this could be seen as an exception, since other fields still have not followed this path. Politics, for instance, is still organized primarily based on nation-states, with the passport being the document that represents national sovereignty and control.

That control works both for citizens within a nation and all others who are outside. It means that all nations would instead collude with a system of travel control that supports freedom of movement. Despite the growing number of restrictions, people have not stopped or reduced their nationalized border crossings. In fact, it is precisely the opposite: today, people are traveling abroad more than ever.

The United Nations Population Division estimates that there is an annual average of 200 million international migrants. In addition, there are almost 10 million stateless people who have been denied nationality and, therefore, denied access to fundamental rights such as education, healthcare, employment, and freedom of movement because of their civic condition. In this sense, considering that freedom of travel is one of the essential marks of the liberated human being, as stated in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the very acceptance of a national passport is incoherent in our globalized era. A world passport is, therefore, a neutral and potential travel identification that challenges conventional ideas about borders and nationalities.

More than 750,000 people have registered to obtain a world passport, which is issued by the World Service Authority (WSA). Many of the applications come from refugees or those who aren’t able to obtain official documents from their own countries. The WSA has also given out thousands of free passports to people in refugee camps.

Creating a world passport, therefore, could be an efficient solution for refugees, one that would allow stateless people to make a new life by changing their legal status. It would redefine equality by positioning it as a relationship among co-members of a global society and not one among national citizens. There is a great deal of discussion and debate within the emerging politics of the No Borders movement. Still, it has been demonstrated that the social division perpetuated by borders is critical when people are characterized as “citizens,” “immigrants,” “refugees,” and so forth.

# Future Perspectives

In the coming decades, we might see new identification documents that will implement the fundamental human right of freedom of travel. With that, the identity document of a global citizen wouldn't be attached to a geographic region, but work in recognition of universal rights: of movement, livelihood, and full and equal societal membership available for everyone. 

If this concept becomes widely accepted by nations, it might change our very core identities, or be seen as a natural next step, following the trend towards easy and fast access to air travel and the digital nomadic lifestyle. It would allow future citizens to move where and when they please, regardless of the migratory restrictions in place nowadays. 

In the perspective of emergency immigration like in the cases of refugees, a cloud-based global passport could be a simplifying and cheap solution for the host nations. The entire make-up of governments and borders could change as people move from place to place in search of a better life. How differently might a world without nationally-bound diplomatic identities look?

description.longTextHtml:
The World Passport consists of a document provided by nonprofit organizations that rely on the human right to travel to give undocumented people actual papers. In a globalized world like ours, we face an increasing degree of convergence between nations in terms of economic thinking and technique. However, this could be seen as an exception, since other fields still have not followed this path. Politics, for instance, is still organized primarily based on nation-states, with the passport being the document that represents national sovereignty and control.

That control works both for citizens within a nation and all others who are outside. It means that all nations would instead collude with a system of travel control that supports freedom of movement. Despite the growing number of restrictions, people have not stopped or reduced their nationalized border crossings. In fact, it is precisely the opposite: today, people are traveling abroad more than ever.

The United Nations Population Division estimates that there is an annual average of 200 million international migrants. In addition, there are almost 10 million stateless people who have been denied nationality and, therefore, denied access to fundamental rights such as education, healthcare, employment, and freedom of movement because of their civic condition. In this sense, considering that freedom of travel is one of the essential marks of the liberated human being, as stated in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the very acceptance of a national passport is incoherent in our globalized era. A world passport is, therefore, a neutral and potential travel identification that challenges conventional ideas about borders and nationalities.

More than 750,000 people have registered to obtain a world passport, which is issued by the World Service Authority (WSA). Many of the applications come from refugees or those who aren’t able to obtain official documents from their own countries. The WSA has also given out thousands of free passports to people in refugee camps.

Creating a world passport, therefore, could be an efficient solution for refugees, one that would allow stateless people to make a new life by changing their legal status. It would redefine equality by positioning it as a relationship among co-members of a global society and not one among national citizens. There is a great deal of discussion and debate within the emerging politics of the No Borders movement. Still, it has been demonstrated that the social division perpetuated by borders is critical when people are characterized as “citizens,” “immigrants,” “refugees,” and so forth.

Future Perspectives

In the coming decades, we might see new identification documents that will implement the fundamental human right of freedom of travel. With that, the identity document of a global citizen wouldn't be attached to a geographic region, but work in recognition of universal rights: of movement, livelihood, and full and equal societal membership available for everyone.

If this concept becomes widely accepted by nations, it might change our very core identities, or be seen as a natural next step, following the trend towards easy and fast access to air travel and the digital nomadic lifestyle. It would allow future citizens to move where and when they please, regardless of the migratory restrictions in place nowadays.

In the perspective of emergency immigration like in the cases of refugees, a cloud-based global passport could be a simplifying and cheap solution for the host nations. The entire make-up of governments and borders could change as people move from place to place in search of a better life. How differently might a world without nationally-bound diplomatic identities look?

description.shortText: Blockchain-based identity protocols that provide a platform to quickly and safely issue, exchange, and verify digital identities.
description.longText:
The traditional identity systems of today are fragmented and, often, exclusive. With the help of the blockchain, which can host and transact unlimited amounts of valued assets through its publicly distributed ledger, identities could be verified on the blockchain and thus be less prone to fraud. The service verifies a person’s multiple social media accounts and past documentation records, thus linking them to their social security number, passport, and other official papers. 

Today, there are different identity issues that governmental systems are not yet ready to address. Data insecurity, for instance, configures a current problem regarding identification. At present, the most valuable identification information is stored on centralized government databases, where it is likely to occur many failure single points. Inaccessibility to prove identity, a common problem faced by immigrants, is another relevant problem showing how those without identification are the most affected. Finally, fraudulent identities evidence the weak link between digital and physical identities, calling out for significant changes regarding identity generating and maintenance systems. 

As a solution, the blockchain enables distributed ledgers to issue and verify significant amounts of documents and assets through smart contracts. It does not demand the user to prove it as the system automatically performs it. Individuals that enter the blockchain database, therefore, could be provided with rights such as opening bank accounts, signing contracts, or applying to university. However, from governments to organizations, a set of standards should be established to consolidate the implementation of digital identity.  

# Future Perspectives

As the gap between the physical and digital world makes identity factors less consistent, it may make it easier for people to create fake identities that generate severe social problems like fake news, for instance. Regarding this and other types of concerns related to democracy and social participation, blockchain and digital identity could be a great pair, helping people by providing a decentralized identity solution. 

Regarding current events related to the refugee crisis, for instance, immigrants could be provided with digital documents to prove their and their families' identities more easily. Host governments and support organizations could start issuing digitally-authenticated identification documents based on the blockchain, as an effort to register and welcome the newcomers. By doing so, governments could enable refugees to feel more integrated into society. Currently, Bitnation can be pointed as an example of a blockchain startup that is helping refugees to obtain digital ID documents, which host governments can use to verify identities.

description.shortText: Adaptive learning dynamically adjusts the way that instructional content is presented to students, based on their responses or preferences. Adaptive learning is increasingly dependent on large-scale collection of learning data and algorithms.

Digital tests is the application of digital technologies to create, grade, administer, report and manage tests and assessment to evaluate what the learner has learned. Digital tests t systems not only include simply making traditional assessments digital, but also using observational, immersive or artificial-intelligence-enhanced capabilities that collect this insight

AI and machine learning are incorporated within threat intelligence and detection solutions, using algorithms to detect patterns and help identify and act upon threats before they can do harm. AI’s ability to adaptively learn and detect novel patterns can accelerate detection, containment, and response, easing the burden on SOC analysts and allowing them to be more proactive.

Chatbots are domain-specific or task-specific conversational interfaces that use an app, messaging platform, social network or chat solution for conversations. Chatbots range in use-case sophistication from simple, decision-tree-based, to implementations built on feature-rich platforms. They are always narrow in scope. A chatbot can be text-based or voice-based, or a combination of both.

A high-level design model in which user & machine interactions primarily occur in the user’s spoken or written natural language. CUIs promise a shift in responsibility between the user and the interface. In traditional UIs, the user operates the technology and is largely responsible for the effects of using it. In a CUI, this responsibility shifts. The CUI is responsible for determining the user’s intention and executing it, meaning the CUI has taken over some of the responsibility from the user.

Education analytics are the collection and analysis of data in education to gain insights, with the goal of improving learning and learning outcomes, services or business practices, and finding new efficiencies, cost savings, and revenue streams.

Digital credentials help with the digitalization of traditional diplomas, alternative micro credentials, professional licensure, certifications and informal credentials that indicate an individual’s knowledge, specialized skills or qualifications via a secure framework to digitally capture and visually present achievements that are verifiable and portable.

Hyflex classrooms or hybrid flexible course, are collaborative teaching spaces that allow faculty to teach students on-campus and online at the same time. Students and faculty are connected using technologies that allow all to be synchronously seen and heard to create a better student engagement environment.
Integrate Smart ID cards with student information systems to automate and digitize attendance, voting, bursary distributions and even access to residence halls and school facilities.

Quantum computing will not displace conventional computers but will disrupt areas such as organic chemistry (batteries), materials science and cryptography (security) where it will deliver results very hard to achieve with traditional methods. Quantum computing will also advance machine learning and optimization solutions in speed and/or quality

A learning experience platform (LEP) is the front-end portal layer that typically sits on top of a learning management system (LMS). LEPs are used to enhance an individual learner’s interactions and engagement via greater personalization, content curation and expanded breadth of content.

RPA solutions to automate back-office, hybrid and student-facing processes with the objective of reducing labor, cost and human error by reliably performing high-volume human tasks. Often the objectives and outcome include an improved student, faculty and staff experience. RPA solutions are also used to automate student transcript requests, and finance management of suppliers and procurement processes.

The VR/AR technologies in education encompasses wide range of applications that range downloading the latest data and display it in an interactive format, to exploring specific equipment and learn how to use it through presenting the required 3D model and helpful explanations which will add practical value to the traditional learning materials.

An app which creates a virtual assistant that can offer round-the-clock, on-demand assistance conveniently to passengers. By looking at an enormous database of commonly asked queries, the core functions of the app are selected to provide passengers with information such as flight information, alerts, things to do around and Lost & Found

Using AR-enabled applications, tourists can use their phones over the objects of interests to generate insights (e.g., information about a certain historical object or site) and translation. This is mainly useful at historical sites where tourists would want to understand certain petroglyph and any type of undeciphered writing.

AI technology has the potentials to sharpen up and enhance the security at the landside area of airports. Existing commercially available systems use a combination of camera, facial recognition and millimeter-wave technologies to scan people walking through a portable security gate. Machine learning techniques are used to automatically analyze data for threats, including explosives and firearms, while ignoring non - dangerous items– for example keys and belt buckles– customers / passengers may be carrying.

AR-enabled applications allow for wayfinding features through which tourist can navigate historical and touristic sites easily. Major sites such as historical sites may not be easy to navigate and therefore, tourists would want an interactive map which helps them experience the sites easily.

Go-style smart check-out combines computer vision and AI to visually track what products the customers select and deselect as they shop. Through delivering convenience and connection in an effortless way, different technologies are implemented such as sensor fusion and computer vision which, once the customer downloads the app and scan it as he/she enters the store, the computer vision cameras  (see) what is in front of them and determine what an object is – to detect when an item has been taken from a shelf by a customer and who has taken it. The system is also able to remove an item from a customer's virtual basket if it is put back on the shelves.

Autonomous Mobile Robot (AMR) are special types of robots can handle delivery and transportation duties to free up staff members' time for customer care. AMRs are equipped with cameras and sensors that allow them to navigate their environment and avoid any unexpected obstacle, such as a crowd of people (e.g., in events, restaurants, symposiums, etc.). AMR is new and innovative ways to improve operational efficiency, enhance speed, ensure precision, and increase safety and can be applied in all sectors, including tourism.

In-store robots are being used to test human-robot interactions. By simply responding to inquiries in several languages, robots can help both tourists and customers locate what they're looking for. Such automated customer service representatives can save up countless hours for human representatives, enabling on-demand assistance. This assistance agent is versatile and adaptive to any environment (i.e., useful for retail, events, airports, and any other large settings).

The hotel robotic assistant is best suited for small and modest B&B accommodations that do not offer a 24-hour concierge service. The robot will act as an on-demand concierge service by offering answers to questions/inquiries from the guests. Anyone may get the information he / she needs from the robotic assistant, whether they have inquiries about F & B recommendations, close - by attractions, or information requests on anything related to the accommodations.

Utilizing IoT and connected motion sensors, largescale events and historical attractions can be well managed through real-time monitoring. By allowing for the monitoring of traffic patterns in events, historical sites, etc. the technology can identify which areas are the busiest and distribute resources accordingly. The data collected from the motion sensors provides better picture of when and where crowds are likely to move which can help derive insights from to help forecast the parking space occupancy, crowd concentrations,among many.

Using IoT, Smart Rooms allow for a full control of the room without the need for human intervention. Guests have the option to control the room such as switching on/off the AC, control the temperature, smart speaker, as well as monitoring the performance of electronic devices remotely, providing hotel staff with live information about their operating status.

Numerous sensors that can detect temperature, humidity, and other factors are the foundation of IoT technology. These sensors may be used to measure both the production state and the shipping time. As a result,F & B organizations are able to actively monitor a variety of data points related to food safety.

Automated gates is a self-service border clearance gates for travelers. The gates are equipped with multiple IOT enabled contact less devices such as iris scanner, palm vein scanner, RFID reader etc. to capture unique passenger data and an analytics engine that compares to collected data with multiple databases to verify the passenger identity.

On-demand aviation refers to the idea of using a ride-hailing service, such as Uber, Lyft and Careem, to book flights in aircraft using electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) technology.The concept is an adaptation of the fractional ownership or charter flight business models currently in use at the upper end of the market.Such business model within the mobility domain could potentially offer a solution to traffic during travel holiday seasons(e.g.Riyadh season).

As the world becomes increasingly connected, and as people travel more for work or leisure, the need for efficient transportation has only grown, real-time luggage tracking has become an essential tool for travelers who want to keep track of their belongings while on the go. Now, with luggage tracking technology becoming more accurate and affordable, it's easier than ever for travelers to keep tabs on their bags, wherever they go.

description.shortText: NFT Art galleries have become a touristic destination for fine arts collectors where it empowers creators who can now reach their customers more directly and get paid more easily. As part of the artistic ecosystem,the authentication and copyrights of the artwork ownership is an essential aspect.Hence the authentication of fine arts using blockchain.

Smart Contracts are contracts that are written as a code enabling the contracts to self-execute once the terms are met. They simplify and automate the process among the tourism value chain and increase overall customer satisfaction. Examples range from “farm to table food traceability”, to identify management to loyalty points redeeming through creating a system of partner network which allows loyalty members to easily earn rewards from multiple providers and exchange them on the network without any cost in the form of “lost” points.

Connected agencies eliminate the departmental boundaries which allow for governments to respond better to complex societal issues. This includes data-sharing which plays a crucial role in the “silo-hacking” effort by becoming a connecting thread between agencies. Silos within and between agencies have long been obstacles to addressing problems, delivering services, and achieving results. Therefore, and in response to the pandemic crisis, governments are creating interagency structures that break down silos and connect government agencies to respond to complex citizen needs.

Life event—based services go further than a single agency focusing on improving the customer interaction. Instead, they represent a realignment and integration of information and resources by understanding and anticipating the cluster of needs a citizen may have. Therefore, life event approach can significantly improve customer experience by offering the appropriate “basket” of services. The cluster of services include (marriage), (New Business),(Employment), (Child Birth)and so on.

Frictionless means that accessing the service requires little to no effort on the part of the beneficiary. They integrate physical and digital worlds across all organizations and are data-driven, and eliminate unnecessary administrative steps. This includes a “one-click” service offering that make it easy to get what you want fast. “The Once-Only) feature allows citizens to get what they need through governments issuing a secure online identification that bridge the gap between agencies without using a single database.Applications include personalized services such as personalized learning whereby educators can now tailor their lessons based on individual' student profiles. In addition, some government entities have also automated, personalized reminders about benefit applications, etc.

Governments have been adopting data-centric technologies and tools such as AI and cloud, but their adoption is often agency-specific and weighed against other priorities and budgetary considerations, making it difficult for agencies to share and act on data effectively.

Unique digital identifiers allow for the integration of data and a seamless citizen experience, enabling massive improvements in service quality, efficiency gains, and the move to a digital delivery model. Unique digital IDs have risks such as connectivity and information sharing.This include data breaches at credit agencies or on social media, failure of technical systems, or concerns over the control and misuse of personal data.Technological failure includes problems with the functionality of the hardware or software associated with a digital ID as well as infrastructure problems.

Total Experience encompasses an end-to-end experience which include CX, UX/UI and EX that transforms the overall business outcome. TX ensures delivering an all-round experience the minute the customer/beneficiary interacts with the service/product, thus breaking silos existing in service offering.
